episode-guide.title: Episode Guide
episode-guide.content:
This page covers every publicly-released main episode of Dark Star Adventurecast, from the crew’s recruitment on Camiri 4 through their discovery of Causeway 3. It’s updated as new episodes go public — if you’re caught up through Episode 29, you’re caught up here too.
Episode 1 — Better a Rat in the Drift…
The crew — hired for a classified operation codenamed “Blackout One” — is assembled on Camiri 4 and receives a pre-recorded briefing from Dr. Elara Voss on behalf of Omnitek Holdings. To recover their new ship, they have to negotiate passage through Drift Rats territory in the docking bays, where gang leader Torik “Rustclaw” Sarr demands a favor before he’ll let them through. Thorne uses a cover identity at the local Gas Mining Office to quietly gather intel while the crew works out how to get free.
Episode 2 — It’s Just a Prank!
As payment for Rustclaw’s favor, the crew hacks the Neon Fangs communication network and plasters Drift Rats insignia across it with the taunt “Better a Rat in the Drift than a King in a Cage.” They christen their newly recovered ship The Scapegoat during a stop at Roger’s Billiards, where death sticks make their first appearance as a recreational drug on the station. When the crew tries to leave, Rustclaw betrays them, and they have to fight their way out in a space chase against two strike fighters, killing Rustclaw in the process.
Episode 3 — Wafisa? I hardly know her!
The crew arrives on Wafisa and lands at Port Ascension, finding the spaceport completely abandoned except for a malfunctioning android help desk. A patrol of the Guardians of the Great Work confronts them, demanding an escalating “toll” before a fight breaks out that leaves two Guardians dead; when more Guardians are later caught trying to blowtorch their way into The Scapegoat, the crew — with Thorne badly wounded and Haleyy knocked to 0 HP — decides they’re too battered to keep fighting and heads instead for Mistretta 4.
Episode 4 — The Methane Switching Station
At Mistretta 4, the crew tries to collect Dr. Elara Voss from her research station, but she initially refuses them entry and instead asks them to restore the gas supply at the Fourth Avenue switching station first. They fight past three Guardian guards to do it — with Haleyy punching straight through a computer terminal along the way — and get the methane flowing again.
Episode 5 — The Glendale Hotel
Their ship is stolen right out from under them, and with Voss confirming that the station’s methane levels are still climbing, the crew takes shelter at the Glendale Hotel. Inside, they find the bodies of Michael and Claire Harrow along with recordings and notes chronicling the Harrows’ account of Wafisa’s collapse — clues that point toward 17 Millbrook Lane and a hidden storage facility.
Episode 6 — The Aurora
Following the Harrows’ notes, the crew finds Millbrook Storage at 17 Millbrook Lane and discovers the Aurora LX-90 hover car hidden behind a false wall. They also trace a mysterious broadcast to the WK9078 Radio Station, where they meet Reginald Froggy Vance and bond with him over music while Felix assesses the damage to his radio tower. Before they part ways, Froggy asks the crew to deliver a message to a contact named Vera Corbin.
Episode 7 — Black Harbor
Viktor Strake arrives on Wafisa with Omnitek soldiers who trace the crew’s earlier hack back to the research station, and Froggy is shot in the crossfire before the crew flees to Blackharbor. There they infiltrate a military airfield — burning through purple flower fields as an entry tactic — to reclaim The Scapegoat, and Thorne kills a clone of Viktor Strake found waiting aboard. The crew is ultimately captured by Omnitek soldiers and loaded into a transport, though Haleyy manages to break free of her bonds along the way.
Episode 8 — Contractually Yours: Scapegoats, Forever
The crew fights their way free and returns to the research station, where Dr. Elara Voss finally reveals her true nature: she is a Virtual Intelligence housed in an alien orb, not the human scientist she appeared to be. She comes clean about the mission being fabricated, lays out her history with Virodyne Labs and Prometheon’s experiments, and offers each crew member a personal reason to keep working with her, plus 20,000 credits. The crew agrees, and The Scapegoat — with Froggy now aboard — sets out on a ten-month journey toward their next destination.
Episode 9 — Brother’s Keeper: Felix’s Story
This focus episode flashes back to Felix Champlin’s past, before he joined the crew: he and his brother Petey Champlin break into Omnitek’s orbital data vault above Polyphn alongside cat burglar Nyx Verhoeven and gunslinger Jett Harlow. Inside, they uncover Operation Red Wing — a program in which Omnitek buys prisoners and converts their consciousness into AI test subjects — and Petey’s mind ends up digitized and trapped on Omnitek’s servers after a confrontation with the digital CEO, Victor Saren. Felix burns his old identity in the aftermath, takes a new name, and resolves to infiltrate Omnitek and rescue his brother, with killing Victor Saren as his driving motivation.
Episode 10 — Rest and Relaxation
The crew stops for fuel at Scrapjack Refueling and Grub in the Orus system, where they meet Yana 7, Dr. Ilon Speth, and Dan Grand — only to discover the Void Cultists have taken over the station and activated a void ansible. Felix hacks the station’s AI, Buddy, for a tactical edge as the crew gets their first look at the Unhallowed and the strange mechanics of void energy.
Episode 11 — Stress and Vexation
The standoff with the Void Cultists escalates further, and in the middle of it Haleyy is singled out and identified as “untethered” — a designation that clearly means something significant to the cultists, though its full weight isn’t yet clear to the crew.
Episode 12 — Death and Damnation
The crew brings the Void Cultists incursion to a head at Scrapjacks, rescuing a captive named Walter and repurposing one of the station’s own turrets against the cultists. They fight through the cult’s leadership, culminating in the death of the Great Brother, and destroy the void rift at the heart of the incursion, ending the crisis. Thorne and Yana 7 end the episode on a romantic note, while Haleyy experiences a disturbing void-touched vision of a worm-like machine and a surfacing, suppressed memory.
Episode 13 — Nexus of Betrayal: Thorne’s Story
This focus episode tells Thorne’s backstory as a rain-soaked neo-noir detective story on Polyphn: Nexus Trading stole his family’s company, Draxus Goods, and Thorne sets out to prove it. He teams up with crash survivor Mara Vex and her bodyguard Brick, along with ex-con muscle Kano Rix, surviving a gravcar chase through Hakumei before assaulting The Relay Tower to pull data proving that Sallerist faked his own death. The mission ends in tragedy — Brick and Kano are killed, Mara is captured, and Thorne’s own mother, Thalia Draxus, reveals that she was the one who really framed him. Thorne had been slated for Red Wing before Voss quietly redirected him to Camiri 4 instead, saving his life.
Episode 14 — The Potential Profit Is…
The crew arrives on Sibylen and meets Vera Corbin, a xenoarchaeologist friend of Froggy’s, at LeCar Research Station. They formally establish Scapegoat Solutions LLC as a legal corporate entity, and Voss activates an alien door for the first time, granting access to Exosite 34b — a buried alien quarantine structure Vera had discovered under the sand. The crew begins exploring inside.
Episode 15 — The Goo Pool
Exploring the upper level of Exosite 34b, the crew watches Voss connect to the alien network she calls the “digital ocean.” Felix submerges himself in a pool of nano fluid and undergoes a knowledge transfer, and in the process the crew senses a massive alien presence somewhere within the network.
Episode 16 — Laser Beams For Eyes!
Deeper in Exosite 34b, the crew passes through a hallway lined with alien vats, each holding a calcified beak, before running into an annihilation bot — a self-replicating, squid-crab hybrid made of nano fluid. Thorne is shot in the fight but patched up with pretech cosmetics, while Felix sprints past the bot to reach a “goo cake” interface and seizes partial control of it, holding it still long enough for the rest of the crew to burn it down before its self-replication can spiral out of control.
Episode 17 — Powering the Nautilus Spiral
The crew descends thirty feet down a goo tube into the exosite’s basement — Haleyy jumps instead of climbing down and takes a hard fall for it — and talks Froggy through a panic attack along the way. They discover the Nautilus Spiral chamber, centered on the alien Paracausal Bifurcation Array pylon, along with a surgical theater lined with empty vats and dormant spider-like surgical bots hanging from the ceiling. Felix uses a goo interface to control the room itself, and Haleyy opens a vat aperture that starts flooding the chamber with nano fluid — just as the surgical bots power on and turn their laser eyes on the crew.
Episode 18 — Elective Surgery
The surgical bots from the previous cliffhanger spring to life immediately. Felix uses the goo interface to slam the ceiling into one bot while Haleyy finishes it off with a bare-fisted haymaker, and Robert Ross rides the second like a bucking bronco before Felix hoists the ceiling — and Robert with it — twenty-two feet into the air. With both bots down, Voss activates the Paracausal Bifurcation Array using the accumulated nano fluid, opening a portal that reveals Prometheon Station — five interlocking rings turning like a celestial gyroscope around a long central rod — with strange blue-diamond shapes resolving into masses of black metal limbs on the other side. Felix and Voss, linked through the goo interface, sense an alien presence with unfathomable intentions, and Haleyy screams and collapses unconscious. While the crew waits out the return trip through the goo tube, Robert begins to open up about his past — hinting at alien tech encountered on Ventos during the Red Rice Wars, and mentioning someone named Haley with one Y.
Episode 19 — The Truth About Haley: Robert’s Story
This focus episode reveals Robert Ross’s true origin: he is clone RR7 from an experimental squadron created by Virodyne Labs through Omnitek Holdings. Flashing back to the Red Rice Wars, Robert and fellow clones Jackal, Envy, and Headcase are sent to Ventos to rescue an elite combat commander named Haley (with one Y) from captivity. Deep in the caves there, an alien fork strikes Haley with energy, turning her eyes from brown to green and singeing her hair; the extraction goes badly wrong, with Headcase killed in the caves and Jackal and Envy killed when an anti-air mech downs their escape helicopter. Haley herself dies of her injuries before Robert’s Lazarus patches can save her, and Robert is later assigned to watch over an amnesiac young woman called “Haleyy” — a reassignment that reroutes him toward Camiri 4 and, eventually, the rest of the crew.
Episode 20 — She Never Existed: Haleyy’s Story
Still unconscious after the fork activation, Haleyy pulls the rest of the crew into her dream, where they play twelve-year-old versions of their characters searching abandoned railroad tracks on BMX bikes for Haleyy’s “missing sister.” After fighting off strange antlered entities in a closing tunnel, they emerge at a dream-version of Virodyne Labs’s laboratories, where a faceless girl and Haleyy’s own vanishing mother lead them deeper into Haleyy’s fractured psyche — including a surgical theater where her private diary pages come alive and attack. In the end, the faceless girl reveals herself as Haley (with one Y), Haleyy’s original identity, and tells her: “your sister is not missing, your sister is not dead — you are an only child.” The two halves merge with a hug, and Haleyy accepts that she and Haley are one and the same. She wakes briefly at the very end, bound and captured along with the rest of the crew, as Viktor Strake leans in: “I had no idea just how valuable you are.”
Episode 21 — Welcome to Your Prison
Viktor Strake captures the crew as they emerge from the exosite, though Thorne manages to invoke InterCorporate law through Scapegoat Solutions LLC to force a temporary 24-hour release. An auction for the rights to Exosite 34b gets underway, but it’s interrupted when the Void Cultists attack and start turning attendees into Unhallowed. In the chaos, Strake locks the crew aboard their own ship using an Omnitek admin override, frying the spike drive and taking Voss captive, while Vera Corbin, Meer Prust, and Sally Gaylen are wired into the Fork in a ritual called the Joining, creating The Concordant. Amid the disaster, Haleyy discovers she has a healing touch.
Episode 22 — Good Job, You Monster
Trapped aboard The Scapegoat after Strake’s lockout, Felix discovers the ship’s ownership module will have to be sourced on the black market before they can regain full control, while Robert and Haleyy pass the time with a hull-denting punching contest. When a Void Cultist vessel attacks, Haleyy mans the weapons station and destroys it, landing a devastating shot on a fleeing cultist ship. The crew finally breaks free onto Sibylen, where Felix finds a note left by Strake confirming that Voss is gone, and the crew sets off toward the Void Cultists’ exosite to find her.
Episode 23 — Pick Up the Box
The crew assaults the Void Cultist exosite to rescue captured Unhallowed, including — to their horror — Froggy himself, now Unhallowed and hauling alien debris under the direction of Rynn Kade of Nexus Trading. A cultist guard named Marun is caught off guard petting the ship’s cat, Percy, near the goo pool room, and is ultimately killed by Haleyy after he refuses to explain Rynn Kade’s presence. Felix seals off Kade’s position in a storage alley with a goo cake, ending the episode on a cliffhanger as he opens peepholes to see what’s inside. Along the way, Haleyy discovers a major new ability: she can verbally command the Unhallowed to perform simple actions, though she can’t yet break them out of their condition — demonstrated by ordering the Unhallowed Froggy to pick up a box.
Episode 24 — Boom! Biosionics!
Haleyy uses her new command ability to safely evacuate the remaining Unhallowed, then leads the crew down to the exosite’s basement, where they find the Fork active — Vera Corbin, Meer Prust, and Sally Gaylen wired into it, with Voss’s orb suspended between its tines. Rynn Kade confronts the crew and reveals that the process merges three humans into a single Virtual Intelligence, and a Void Cultist named Kethrix identifies Thorne as a “candidate” and Haleyy as “untethered” before Robert shoots him dead mid-monologue. In the fight that follows, Kade shoots Thorne down to 0 HP from concealment before Robert kills her in turn, and with no healing available, Haleyy discovers she has latent biosionic healing powers just in time to save Thorne’s life, collapsing from the effort. The Fork process completes regardless — Vera, Meer, and Sally all die, and the orb that descends from it becomes The Concordant.
Episode 25 — Rock Tumor
The crew arrives at The Spigot looking for medical help for Haleyy and a black-market ownership module for The Scapegoat. Dr. Iso scans Haleyy and finds crystalline structures growing in her frontal lobe, though neither she nor Felix — who theorizes the crystals are a residual artifact of the Fork overload channeling energy through her — can say for certain what it means. Iso leads them to The Vent bar to find Peter Haslow, a bot mechanic who deals in ownership modules, and Thorne charms him into revealing that the next shipment lands at Helium Docks #7 at 3am. A grenade attack at the bar — smothered by Robert before it can do worse damage, though the bartender is killed — leads to a stranger discovery back at Iso’s shop: Felix recognizes her resemblance to Robert and realizes Dr. Iso is herself a clone of Robert’s line. With Thorne suspecting Viktor Strake sent the attacker, the crew sets a plan to hit the Helium Docks shipment at 3am.
Episode 26 — You’re a Good Person, Robert
Tracing the grenade attacker to a docked Omnitek ship, the crew breaches it with one of Iso’s flashbangs and finds yet another Robert-line clone aboard, designated DT7X. He reveals he’d been tracking The Scapegoat using leftover Omnitek admin codes buried in the ship’s systems and was waiting in The Spigot on orders — but before Thorne can finish interrogating him about the command structure behind it all, Iso shoots him dead. A dead man’s transponder activates as he dies, alerting an unseen partner who never shows up to retaliate. Afterward, Robert Ross and Haleyy finally have the long-deferred conversation about his lies, her identity, and what really happened on Ventos.
Episode 27 — Life Is Unfair
Felix finishes hacking the derelict Omnitek ship and learns the crew’s standing orders were recently upgraded from “follow” to “eliminate.” Back at The Spigot, Dr. Iso’s shop turns out to have been bombed, with another Robert-line clone found dead inside — killed by her own automated turret — and the loss pushes Iso to fully commit to the crew’s fight. That night, the crew hits the Helium Docks compound to steal the incoming ownership module shipment, fighting off armed security drones during the handoff and a road ambush on the way out before making it back to The Scapegoat with the module in hand. Dr. Iso officially joins the crew as one of their own, and Felix reinstalls Buddy AI as the ship’s managing VI now that Voss is gone.
Episode 28 — I’m Not Angry, I’m Disappointed
Felix uncovers coordinates Voss hid inside one of Strake’s own transmissions, pointing the crew toward an unlisted station called Causeway 3, eighteen days away by spike drive. Before they leave, Dr. Iso gives Haleyy a grim update: the crystalline growth in her brain will fully consume it within about six months, though Iso notes something about Haleyy is resisting the process in a way she hasn’t seen before. During the long transit, the crew settles into quieter routines — Froggy withdraws into his nest, Robert watches the dark, Thorne paces the corridors — before arriving at an empty, dim system where Causeway 3 flags their ship’s ownership module and denies them entry. Felix forces his way in through an exterior spacewalk and a hack, and once aboard the crew bluffs and hacks their way past security — with Thorne impersonating Strake to fool a human monitoring officer — to confirm that The Acceptable Loss delivered Voss to Prometheon Station. Just as they get the confirmation, a security patrol announces its intent to destroy The Scapegoat and swarms of security drones burst out to attack.
Episode 29 — Eleven Rounds
Swarms of electro-beetle robots erupt from the walls as Felix races to finish his hack, with Thorne, Haleyy, and Robert forming a defensive perimeter around him — Thorne takes repeated heavy hits protecting Felix and is left at just 2 of 12 HP. Felix’s hack confirms that The Acceptable Loss carried Strake and Voss to Prometheon Station, and turns up an older, deeper trail: an Omnitek data vault that also passed through Causeway 3 years earlier, bound for Prometheon, and never returned. With the drones closing in, Robert clears a path back to The Scapegoat and the crew cycles through the airlock and reaches their stations with rounds to spare, spike-drilling toward Prometheon Station with Buddy setting the course. A security patrol hails them over comms, having identified the ship through outstanding warrants, and demands they stand down; the crew fakes comms trouble and stonewalls, but the patrol’s faster ship keeps closing the gap as the episode ends.

factions/auctioneers-guild.title: Auctioneers Guild
factions/auctioneers-guild.content:
The Auctioneers Guild is a sector-wide neutral body that facilitates the transfer of contested assets — alien exosites, xeno-archaeology finds, liquidated research firms, and anything else that would spark inter-corporate conflict without a neutral third party involved. It belongs to no corporation and answers to none of them, not Virodyne Labs, Nexus Trading, or any other power operating in the Viridian Expanse.
The Guild’s mandate is to run auctions and process asset transfers, taking a cut of every transaction. Nearly every inter-corporate deal in the sector runs through it in some form, from formal auctions down to private ship sales.
The Guild has no standing army, only guards. Its power is entirely soft, resting on three pillars: every major corporation depends on access to its auctions, so none can afford to move against it without the others intervening; it keeps an audit log of every transaction it has ever processed, which gives it quiet leverage simply by existing; and any corporation caught violating auction neutrality can be banned from future bidding, a punishment no corporation can afford.
The Guild operates everywhere corporations do business, including Sibylen, with representatives recognizable by their ceremonial robes.
Key Representatives
Meer Prust is the Second High Auctioneer Representative for Sibylen, with offices in The Spigot.
Campaign Appearances

Ep 21: Meer Prust arrived during Viktor Strake’s interrogation of the crew of The Scapegoat, forcing Strake to release them for 24 hours so a Guild auction could proceed, and backed Thorne’s legal argument. Prust then conducted the auction for Exosite 34b.


Appears in: Ep 21

factions/drift-rats.title: Drift Rats
factions/drift-rats.content:
The Drift Rats are a gang holding Docking Bays 50-80 on Camiri 4, behind a barricaded entry point. Roughly 28 members strong, they mostly use their territory as a hideout, committing crimes elsewhere and retreating behind their barricade to stay safe. Their symbol is a red rat on a green-and-yellow field, and their motto is “Better a Rat in the Drift than a King in a Cage.” Guards wear hacked-together green-and-yellow armor with matching mohawks.
Their emblem is nearly identical to that of the Neon Fangs, another Camiri 4 gang — the two may have splintered from a common origin.
The crew of The Scapegoat stored their ship in Drift Rats territory early on. The gang’s leader, Torik “Rustclaw” Sarr, ultimately betrayed the crew by trying to steal the ship for himself, sending two strike fighters in pursuit as the Scapegoat fled Camiri 4. Rustclaw died in the attempt.

factions/faction-overview.title: Faction Overview
factions/faction-overview.content:
The Viridian Expanse is dominated by a handful of interlocking mega-corporations, alongside independent operators, military powers, gangs, and cults that the crew of The Scapegoat has encountered in the course of their travels.
Corporate Hierarchy
Virodyne Labs sits atop a hidden corporate empire, secretly controlling Kinetika Dynamics (weapons technology), Prometheon Technologies (dark energy and antimatter research, which in turn controls Nexus Trading), and Omnitek Holdings (planetary mining and prisoner-contract labor). None of these subsidiaries publicly advertise their connection to Virodyne.
Independent Corporations

Laicar Research — xenoarchaeology, based on Sibylen
Blackout Press — underground journalism, sector-wide
Auctioneers Guild — neutral asset auctions, based on Sibylen

Military / Political

Guardians of the Great Work — military dictatorship controlling Blackharbor and the ruins of Wafisa
The Saltborn — the rebellion opposing them in Blackharbor

Gangs

Drift Rats — roughly 28 members, Camiri 4
Neon Fangs — roughly 85 members, Camiri 4

Cults

Void Cultists — seek “void ascension,” encountered at Scrapjacks and Sibylen

The Crew

Scapegoat Solutions LLC — the legal business entity founded by Thorne to give the crew standing in a corporation-dominated sector

Known Relationships

Virodyne Labs secretly controls Kinetika Dynamics, Prometheon Technologies (and by extension Nexus Trading), and Omnitek Holdings
Guardians of the Great Work and The Saltborn are locked in open conflict over Blackharbor
Drift Rats and Neon Fangs are rivals for territory on Camiri 4
Viktor Strake, acting for Virodyne, has pursued the crew of The Scapegoat since early in their travels


Appears in: Ep 1, 2, 4, 7, 8, 17, 21

factions/guardians-of-the-great-work.title: Guardians of the Great Work
factions/guardians-of-the-great-work.content:
The Guardians of the Great Work are a zealot military force clinging to the dream of restoring the gas industry in the ruins of Wafisa’s megacity. They seize wealth, fuel, and manpower from Blackharbor, promising that the “Great Work” will one day be complete and prosperity will follow. Their symbol is a golden shield with an abstract pointed logo, and their catchphrase is “For the good of the work.”
The Guardians number somewhere between 500 and 2,500 soldiers, based out of the Guardian Compound in Blackharbor — a half-mile-square fortress of concrete and steel with walls, watchtowers, and automated turrets. Their airfield, once large, has been bombed down to a quarter of its former size, with three active landing strips.
Their methods are brutal: heavy taxation under threat of severe punishment, forced labor squads sent to distant projects that many never return from, conscription of Blackharbor citizens, and seizure of crops, fuel, and batteries. Officers live in comfort while civilians starve. Guardian troops wear battered armor with golden shields and winged helmets, armed with laser rifles and shock knives.

factions/kinetika-dynamics.title: Kinetika Dynamics
factions/kinetika-dynamics.content:
Kinetika Dynamics is a weapons and armor manufacturer operating as a subsidiary of Virodyne Labs. It keeps a low profile, working mostly in the background of Virodyne’s operations. Its weapons technology was used in experiments on Dr. Elara Voss’s homeworld, and Kinetika-supplied weapons and armor equipped the experimental clone squadron — including Robert Ross — deployed to Ventos.

Appears in: Ep 19

factions/laicar-research.title: Laicar Research
factions/laicar-research.content:
Laicar Research is a corporation focused on xenoarchaeology, primarily active on Sibylen. The corporation discovered Exosite 34b, the alien quarantine building that became central to the crew’s business on Sibylen.
Notable Members
Vera Corbin worked for Laicar as a xenoarchaeologist on Sibylen.
Relationships
Laicar Research is a client of Scapegoat Solutions LLC under a legally binding contract. In Episode 17, Thorne used that contract as leverage, arguing the crew were technically Laicar employees to force Viktor Strake to release them for 24 hours. Laicar also competed at auction against Virodyne Labs and Novacrypt Solutions.

Appears in: Ep 17

factions/neon-fangs.title: Neon Fangs
factions/neon-fangs.content:
The Neon Fangs are a gang controlling the docking bays from the low 40s down to bay 20 on Camiri 4. Despite the “gang” label, they’re genuinely good people — a community that has organized itself for mutual protection and commerce. Their territory is essentially a giant open-air market, with stalls, merchants, residents, hostels, and even a shanty town. Roughly 85 members strong, they wear red-and-black spray-painted armor and carry a red rat with two fangs as their symbol — an emblem nearly identical to that of the rival Drift Rats, suggesting the two gangs may share a common origin.
Guards are polite and keep order, functioning less like criminals and more like a community police force protecting their own from the more dangerous Drift Rats and other threats. The Neon Fangs invited the crew of The Scapegoat to join their collective.

factions/nexus-trading.title: Nexus Trading
factions/nexus-trading.content:
Nexus Trading is a long-haul trading corporation, a subsidiary of Prometheon Technologies (itself controlled by Virodyne Labs). Its own subsidiary, Draxus Goods, is officially a textile manufacturing and distribution company headquartered in Hakumei Prefecture on Polyphn — but it also trades in alien artifacts recovered from Wafisa.

factions/omnitek-holdings.title: Omnitek Holdings
factions/omnitek-holdings.content:
Omnitek Holdings is a relatively new corporation that has grown by purchasing prison inmates to serve out their sentences on contract, alongside ordinary non-prisoner contracts. It is secretly owned by Virodyne Labs. Its insignia is gold, and it employs roughly 5,000 workers across administration, manual labor, engineering, security, and special operations.
Behind its public face, Omnitek runs Operation Red Wing: it buys prisoner contracts at double the going rate, converts the prisoners’ consciousness into AI test subjects (killing them in the process), and runs the resulting AIs through nightmare simulations. This program was uncovered by Felix Champlin and his brother during a heist on Omnitek’s orbital data vault above Polyphn.
Omnitek also ran a clone program that produced an experimental squadron of soldiers — including Robert Ross — fitted with Kinetika Dynamics weapons and armor. That program was scrapped after the disaster on Ventos. Separately, Omnitek is digging for ancient alien technology deep beneath the surface of Polyphn using contracted laborers.

factions/prometheon-technologies.title: Prometheon Technologies
factions/prometheon-technologies.content:
Prometheon Technologies is a subsidiary of Virodyne Labs specializing in dark-energy and antimatter research. Much of what Virodyne does in genetics is backed by Prometheon’s research. The corporation’s headquarters is a secret space station somewhere in deep space, its exact location classified — described as interlocking rings, like a “Celestial Gyroscope,” pierced by a long central rod.
The station briefly became visible to the crew through an alien relay on Sibylen when the alien Fork technology there was activated.
Relationships
Prometheon is a subsidiary of Virodyne Labs. Dr. Elara Voss, the VI who recruited the crew, has expressed hostility toward the station and its operations.

Appears in: Ep 17

factions/scapegoat-solutions-llc.title: Scapegoat Solutions LLC
factions/scapegoat-solutions-llc.content:
Scapegoat Solutions LLC is the crew’s own legal business entity, created by Thorne using his knowledge of corporate law. It serves as their legal identity in a sector dominated by corporations, giving them standing to make contracts, hold property, and negotiate on equal footing with the megacorporations around them.
Members

Thorne — Founder / legal representative
Haleyy
Robert Ross
Felix Champlin

Legal Uses
In Episode 17, Thorne used InterCorporate policy to argue that the crew were technically Laicar Research employees under a legally binding contract with Scapegoat Solutions LLC, forcing Viktor Strake to release them for 24 hours.

Appears in: Ep 17

factions/the-saltborn.title: The Saltborn
factions/the-saltborn.content:
The Saltborn are the rebellion operating within Blackharbor — a loose network of smugglers, dissidents, and saboteurs fighting against the rule of the Guardians of the Great Work. Their name reflects the belief that Blackharbor’s people, born of salt and sea, should never bow to tyrants.

factions/virodyne-labs.title: Virodyne Labs
factions/virodyne-labs.content:
Virodyne Labs is the sector’s dominant mega-corporation — a genetics, cloning, and disease-control company whose public face is respectable corporate governance. Behind the scenes, it secretly controls a web of subsidiaries, including Kinetika Dynamics, Prometheon Technologies (which in turn controls Nexus Trading), and Omnitek Holdings. Virodyne’s uniform is black with white trim.
Virodyne experiments on human populations, runs prisoner conversion programs, manufactures weapons through its subsidiaries, and pursues alien technology by any means available.
Notable Members

Virodyne’s presence spans Polyphn (through Omnitek), a secret deep-space station (through Prometheon), and the world where Dr. Elara Voss’s early experiments were conducted.
Relationships
Virodyne controls Kinetika Dynamics, Prometheon Technologies, and Omnitek Holdings, along with their own subsidiaries. It counts Dr. Elara Voss and the crew of The Scapegoat among its enemies. Its reach extends to the Void Cultists as well — a connection uncovered through Rynn Kade at Nexus Trading during the Sibylen auction in Episode 17.

factions/void-cultists.title: Void Cultists
factions/void-cultists.content:
The Void Cultists are a religious cult seeking “ascension” through rituals involving void energy. They use void ansibles — strange devices that tear rifts in spacetime — to expose people to void energy, creating Unhallowed: mindless, husk-like creatures the cult can direct. Somehow, the cult can also read the ancient “dots and swirls” alien language.
The cult is organized hierarchically, with titles including Brother, Sister, Hierophant, Adept, Tollbearer, Archivist, and Mother. Members wear gray-and-black mottled robes; many are bald with face and neck tattoos, and carry shotguns, laser pistols, or chainsaw-blade swords.
Unhallowed and Untethered
When the cult exposes someone to void energy, one of two things happens. Unhallowed are people the void energy hits without anything “connecting” — they become mindless husks the cult directs for combat, labor, or logistics; whether any consciousness remains inside is unconfirmed. Untethered are people the void reaches and something in them connects; they survive with some kind of relationship to the void and are seen by the cult as candidates for what they call the Great Ascension, their ultimate goal of transcending galactic life. An untethered person can command the unhallowed directly, but cannot command someone out of being unhallowed — whether that state is reversible at all is unknown.
An untethered person outside the cult is either someone the cult wants to recruit, or a threat to deal with. Haleyy has had multiple void contacts and is confirmed untethered by the cult’s own definition.
Notable Members

Locations
The cult took over the Scrapjacks truck stop (Ep 10-11) and attacked the auction at Exosite 34b on Sibylen (Ep 17). Their ship is a large, brutalist, black-and-gray vessel patched together from other ships’ parts, unable to survive atmospheric entry, with a cargo hold that has carried sleeping Unhallowed.
Technology
The cult’s void ansible (or rift device) is a five-foot antenna with forked prongs that opens a growing rift, corrupting minds and bodies within roughly a five-meter radius; destroying the device stops the mental control but not the physical corruption already inflicted. The material doesn’t feel like metal — it “gives,” as if organic. The cultists also carry two-tined forks, crude replicas of genuine alien technology, and can read the alien “dots and swirls” script by means still unexplained.
Relationships
The cult is linked to Nexus Trading (through Rynn Kade), which in turn ties back to Virodyne Labs. Beyond that connection, the cult counts nearly everyone else as an enemy.

Appears in: Ep 10, 11, 17, 23

items/harrow-family-cookbook.title: Harrow Family Cookbook
items/harrow-family-cookbook.content:
The Harrow Family Cookbook is a red notebook containing recipes spanning three generations of the Harrow family, found at 17 Millbrook Lane on Wafisa. It has roughly 100 blank pages in the back. The book belonged to Michael and Claire Harrow, whose bodies were found at the Glendale Hotel.
Haleyy has carried the cookbook with her ever since, the same way the crew treasures The Aurora — a small, human touchstone amid the rest of their travels.

Appears in: Ep 5, 6, 25 (SML)

items/lokipon-cards.title: Lokipon Cards
items/lokipon-cards.content:
Lokipon is an in-universe collectible card game, similar in spirit to Magic: The Gathering or Pokémon. Decks and cards turn up scattered through the campaign, first found at the Glendale Hotel and 17 Millbrook Lane on Wafisa, including pre-built decks discovered in a child’s bedroom.
The game has become a running bit of levity for the crew, who collect the cards obsessively in-game. Thorne and Robert Ross are its most enthusiastic players and collectors, while Haleyy keeps a deck in her bunk mostly to practice, despite not being very good at it.
Rules
The rules have been improvised collaboratively at the table as the game recurs. What’s been established so far: the goal is to avoid catching any Lokipon — the creatures want an owner and are constantly trying to attach themselves to someone, but a Lokipon distracts from real life and drains funds. The win condition is to make an opponent catch a Lokipon instead; whoever ends up stuck with one loses. Trap cards can force this on an opponent. Known Lokipon include “Danger Pa,” and known card types include Terria, a kind of mana.

Appears in: Ep 3, 5, 6

items/the-aurora.title: The Aurora
items/the-aurora.content:
The Aurora (LX-90) is a plutonium-powered hover car — essentially a nuclear-powered two-door sports car — discovered behind a false wall in storage bay 17 at Millbrook Storage on Wafisa, following instructions left behind by Michael Harrow at the Glendale Hotel. Despite years of abandonment, it’s still fully operational thanks to its nuclear power source.
The car held personal effects from the Harrow family, including a photograph and a leather jacket that Thorne later claimed for himself. It’s now stored in The Scapegoat’s cargo hold, sharing space with Reginald “Froggy” Vance’s living quarters.
The Aurora also appeared in one of Haleyy’s dreams, in which her mother was seated in a crashed version of the car.

Appears in: Ep 6, 16

items/vehicles.title: Vehicles
items/vehicles.content:
An index of ground, air, and small space vehicles the crew has encountered. Ships with spike drives — capable of interstellar travel — have their own entries: The Scapegoat, The Kid, The Thalia, and The Acceptable Loss.
Crew Vehicle

locations/camiri-4/drift-rats-territory.title: Drift Rats Territory
locations/camiri-4/drift-rats-territory.content:
Drift Rats Territory occupies Docking Bays 50-80 on Camiri 4, held by the Drift Rats gang. It has a single point of entry, barricaded and guarded at all times, with scorch marks lining the walls. The barricades are built from stacked storage bins and metal sheeting, watched by two armed guards in hacked-together armor painted bright green and yellow and decorated with the gang’s red rat emblem.
Inside, the territory is mostly large and empty docking bays, though a few strike fighters sit ready for use. It functions as a clubhouse for the gang, who commit crimes elsewhere and retreat here to stay safe — about a dozen Drift Rats are present at any given time.
The crew had to negotiate passage through here to reach The Scapegoat (Ep 1-2). Gang leader Torik Rustclaw Sarr offered them passage in exchange for hacking the Neon Fangs’ network. The ship was stored in this territory before the crew claimed it.

Appears in: Ep 1, Ep 2

locations/camiri-4/gas-mining-front.title: Gas Mining Front
locations/camiri-4/gas-mining-front.content:
The Gas Mining Front is a fake recruiting office for a gas mining company on Camiri 4 — the only Omnitek Holdings location on the station. It served as a cover for Omnitek’s operations, and it’s where the crew received their initial mission briefing via a pre-recorded message (Ep 1). The briefing directed them to pick up Dr. Elara Voss on Wafisa and investigate a mysterious signal.

Appears in: Ep 1

locations/camiri-4/neon-fangs-territory/.title: Roger's Billiards
locations/camiri-4/neon-fangs-territory/.content:
Roger’s Billiards is a pool hall in Neon Fangs Territory on Camiri 4, owned by Neon Fangs guard Roger Neronta and run day-to-day by his wife Cecelia and son Axle. It has five pool tables with room for around fifty people, a long metal bar with no front paneling, and an old-world jukebox modified to play hits from the station’s notable artists. The space is cluttered but clean, decorated with paintings, beaded curtains, badges, and stickers. A storage room in back is accessible by hand-wave sensor and leads to the bathrooms, and a keypad-locked door connects to an adjacent room with a computer terminal and security camera.

Appears in: Ep 2

locations/camiri-4/neon-fangs-territory/.title: Neon Fangs Territory
locations/camiri-4/neon-fangs-territory/.content:
Neon Fangs Territory occupies Docking Bays 22-43 on Camiri 4, controlled by the Neon Fangs gang. It’s a long, wide, open corridor patrolled by gang members, functioning essentially as a giant open-air market where people from all over the station come to trade. Most of the smaller docking bays here have been converted into businesses, including Roger’s Billiards, a pool hall owned by Roger Neronta.
The crew passed through here during their escape from Camiri 4 (Ep 1-2). Felix hacked the Neon Fangs’ communication network and plastered Drift Rats insignia across every screen with the message: “Better a Rat in the Drift than a King in a Cage.”

Appears in: Ep 1, Ep 2

locations/camiri-4/_camiri-4.title: Camiri 4
locations/camiri-4/_camiri-4.content:
Camiri 4 is a highly populated space station in the Schroeter system, orbiting the gas giant Camiri. It is ruled by martial law and carved up into sections controlled by various gangs, mafias, and policed communities. Once a hub for research and development, it has spent the past twenty years becoming a haven for black market drugs and illicit activity.
The station’s corridors are dirty and grimy, organized by numbered docking bay sections, with the air smelling of rust and old fuel and malfunctioning lights flickering overhead. A simulated day/night cycle dims the lights on a timer and warms their color toward evening. There is no governing authority — pure anarchy rules the station.
In its prime, Camiri 4 was a bustling hub of activity, the launching-off point for scientific and industrial ventures headed into the southern and southeastern outer reaches of civilized space. Scientists and adventurers used it as a base for exploring new worlds, and Omnitek Holdings and other corporations kept a foothold here. About twenty years ago, a rebellion on the station left many dead and pushed all corporate interests out — it was simply too dangerous to stay. The station became overrun by independent factions, like the Drift Rats, who carved out their own territory, and the corporations decided it wasn’t worth the trouble of retaking.
The station is located on the “south side” of Polyphn, off to the east — the opposite direction from Sibylen in the outer reaches of civilized space.
Sub-locations include the Drift Rats’ territory in Docking Bays 50-80, the Neon Fangs’ territory in Docking Bays 22-43, Roger’s Billiards within Neon Fangs territory, and the Gas Mining Front, a fake Omnitek recruiting office and the only Omnitek presence on the station.
The crew was recruited here via an Omnitek pre-recorded briefing (Ep 1). They had to negotiate with the Drift Rats to reach their ship, hacking the Neon Fangs’ network as payment (Ep 2), and named the ship The Scapegoat. Their departure was contested by a space battle with two strike fighters (Ep 2).

Appears in: Ep 1, Ep 2

locations/camiri.title: Camiri
locations/camiri.content:
Camiri is an uninhabited gas giant in the Schroeter system. Over the years, four space stations were built in its orbit, numbered sequentially as they were constructed.
Camiri 1 was destroyed after its orbit decayed and it fell into the planet. Camiri 2 is a derelict currently in a decaying orbit, on the same trajectory toward destruction — extremely dangerous to approach. Camiri 3 is derelict and abandoned but sits in a stable orbit, making it safe to visit, though nobody is known to have done so. Camiri 4 is the only active station, a gang-controlled anarchy and the starting location of the crew’s campaign.

Appears in: Ep 1

locations/causeway-3.title: Causeway 3
locations/causeway-3.content:
Causeway 3 is a secret Virodyne routing station the crew reached after decoding hidden coordinates from Strake’s outgoing transmission — pulses buried in a carrier wave, mechanical chirps that only Felix recognized. The coordinates led to an unnamed system three jumps out, an eighteen-day transit away (Ep 28).
Exterior: A short cylinder studded with dense antenna arrays on every surface, a flat docking ring facing inbound traffic, and turret ports recessed into the outer hatch, only visible up close.
Docking hallway: A zero-G corridor running the station’s length, its walls pitted with hidden slots that deploy optical lens and laser tracking arrays when intruders enter (targeting only, unarmed). The inner end holds a voice-controlled comms panel.
Server room: A tight hexagonal space with terminals ringing every wall and indicator lights throughout. Slots along the floor and ceiling can launch security drone swarms if a hack is detected, with one main interface terminal on the right wall.
When the crew arrived, the station immediately flagged their ship’s ownership module as unauthorized and warned that authorities had been notified. Felix spacewalked to an exterior control panel while Haleyy held his line, hacking the docking clamps open. The crew entered in vac suits as camera arrays tracked them; Thorne successfully bluffed a human security officer monitoring the comms into opening the inner door. Felix then hacked the server terminal and cleared the outer security layer, uncovering transit logs confirming that Strake’s ship, the Acceptable Loss, had delivered Voss to Prometheon Station — the first hard confirmation of her location since her capture. As the hack continued, a security patrol was flagged inbound and drone swarms began deploying from the walls, ending the episode on a cliffhanger (Ep 28).
Picking up mid-hack, three drone swarms pressed Felix from multiple flanks while the rest of the crew held the line against an approaching patrol vessel. Deeper in the system, Felix’s hack turned up a second discovery: historical records showing that the Omnitek data vault — carrying Petey’s digitized consciousness — had also transited through Causeway 3 years earlier, bound for Prometheon Station, and never returned. The drill-path directory also exposed an unlisted, unexplored destination alongside the Prometheon route. With the drill path to Prometheon Station in hand, the crew fought off the drones, escaped back to their ship, and fled the station under pursuit (Ep 29).

Appears in: Ep 28, Ep 29

locations/pare.title: Pare
locations/pare.content:
Pare is a desert night world in the Anagris system, perpetually dark with cold winds scouring a barren landscape. A mining colony was established here but failed due to hostile wildlife; its ruins remain, though nobody has reason to go back. Scrap Jack’s Refueling and Grub, a truck stop station, orbits nearby.

Appears in: Ep 10

locations/polyphn/hakumei-prefecture/blo.title: Bloc 6
locations/polyphn/hakumei-prefecture/blo.content:
Bloc 6 is a residential district on Polyphn where Mara Vex and Brick grew up, containing multi-story residential towers. The Bloc had its own gangs, with Brick serving as an enforcer for one.
A private maglev carrying William Sallerist and five others derailed and crashed into a Bloc 6 residential tower, officially killing all five occupants and twelve residents and injuring dozens more. Nexus Trading officers arrived on scene almost instantly and killed survivors they found. Mara Vex’s entire family was killed in the crash; she barely escaped.

Appears in: Ep 12

locations/polyphn/hakumei-prefecture/clu.title: Club KuroLuxe
locations/polyphn/hakumei-prefecture/clu.content:
Club KuroLuxe is a nightclub in Hakumei Prefecture on Polyphn. Neon light spills from its entrance in blues, reds, and purples, flickering through the alley like a broken memory, bass thumping through the walls as a nearby vent hisses steam.
Thorne and Kano Rix met Mara Vex and Brick in the alley behind the club after receiving an anonymous message: “Sallerist lives. He’s been erased. Meet in the alley behind KuroLuxe. Midnight. Bring muscle.” Two Nexus Trading goons ambushed them with shock batons, and Mara and Brick arrived in a battered gravcar, launching a high-speed chase (Ep 12).

Appears in: Ep 12

locations/polyphn/hakumei-prefecture/dr..title: Dr. Sial's Clinic
locations/polyphn/hakumei-prefecture/dr..content:
Dr. Sial’s Clinic is a ripperdoc clinic deep in Polyphn’s underground, accessible through service tunnels and forgotten corridors beneath Hakumei Prefecture. The air is stale and heavy with ozone; a rusted door marked with a faded red cross leads inside. The clinic is cramped and cluttered with cybernetic parts and flickering monitors, surgical arms hanging overhead like dormant insects.
After the gravcar chase, Mara Vex led the group here to lay low and regroup. Dr. Sial, an old ally of Mara’s, patched up the group and ran diagnostics on her bio-mods, showing that he could remotely see through her telescopic eye — the clue that revealed he had secretly been reporting to Nexus Trading all along (Ep 12).

Appears in: Ep 12

locations/polyphn/hakumei-prefecture/the.title: The Relay Tower
locations/polyphn/hakumei-prefecture/the.content:
The Relay Tower is a skeletal antenna tower looming against the haze of Polyphn’s upper sprawl in Hakumei Prefecture — an ancient, rust-streaked structure with exposed steel lower levels, forgotten scaffolds, and open-air platforms bolted onto the frame. Cables whip and hum in the wind, hazard lights flicker through the gloom, and faded Nexus Corp logos cling to the metal, half-eaten by rust. It’s one of many automated data relays that funnel Nexus Corp communications, each keeping a rolling seven-day cache of every transmission before permanent erasure.
The relay nearest the Bloc 6 crash site was taken offline for “repairs” hours after the maglev derailment and never came back online — its cache contained the command that crashed the maglev, proving William Sallerist had faked his death. Thorne climbed the tower while Mara Vex, Brick, and Kano Rix fought off Nexus forces below. At the top, Thorne encountered his mother, Thalia Draxus, who revealed that she herself had framed him, not Sallerist alone. A Nexus skimmer and van attacked during the data extraction; Brick and Kano were killed in the fight, and Mara was taken (Ep 12).

Appears in: Ep 12

locations/polyphn/hakumei-prefecture/_ha.title: Hakumei Prefecture
locations/polyphn/hakumei-prefecture/_ha.content:
Hakumei Prefecture is one of many prefectures on the ultra-urbanized surface of Polyphn — rain-slicked metal walkways, plasteel grates, and neon-drenched alleys, the air smelling of burnt synth oil and soy noodles, sub-orbital skyways humming overhead.
It’s home to Nexus Trading headquarters and the site of Thorne’s Episode 12 flashback adventure. Notable features include Club KuroLuxe, a nightclub used as an alley meeting point; Dr. Sial’s Clinic, a ripperdoc clinic in the underground; The Relay Tower, a decommissioned Nexus data relay antenna; Bloc 6, a residential district destroyed in a staged maglev crash; an Omnitek barracks used for worker housing; and a retro-café where Thorne first researched William Sallerist on his datapad.
Thorne roamed Hakumei tracking down William Sallerist, meeting Mara Vex in the alley behind Club KuroLuxe, surviving a gravcar chase through the streets, retreating to Dr. Sial’s Clinic in the underground, and joining an assault on The Relay Tower by Nexus forces, where his mother Thalia Draxus revealed the truth about Sallerist’s betrayal (Ep 12).

Appears in: Ep 12

locations/polyphn/_polyphn.title: Polyphn
locations/polyphn/_polyphn.content:
Polyphn is a night world in the Lebima system with a hyper-urbanized surface — a pulsing patchwork quilt of civilization, neon streaks and suborbital skyways humming with life. Buildings cover most of the land mass and extend dozens of levels below the surface.
Polyphn orbits its sun at the extreme far reaches of the gravity well, so little light reaches it that daylight barely registers, and a dense layer of industrial smog filters out whatever UV might otherwise get through. The planet runs entirely on artificial light — streetlights, neon signs, and building illumination dominate the visual landscape at all times — and it seems to always be raining. Deep underground, service tunnels and forgotten corridors house unhoused populations that the police won’t enter.
Polyphn is home to Omnitek Holdings headquarters and the majority of its workforce, roughly 5,000 workers, mostly laborers mining deep below the surface. Dozens of smaller stations, satellites, and orbital platforms crowd the space around the planet.
The surface is divided among major corporations, each owning country-sized regions. Virodyne Laboratories owns roughly half the planet; within its territory, Omnitek Holdings controls about a third, and Nexus Trading owns a state-sized region that includes Hakumei Prefecture. Neighborhoods within each section are organized into numbered “Blocs,” with block numbers repeating between sections. Other corporations hold smaller territories elsewhere. No nature is visible anywhere — dirt, cement, and twisted steel grates, with acidic rain crashing down constantly in some districts.
Surface locations include Hakumei Prefecture, with its nightclub, ripperdoc clinic, and The Relay Tower, as well as Bloc 6, a residential district destroyed in a staged maglev crash. In orbit sit the public Polyphn Station, Omnitek Holdings’ The Orbital Data Vault, a Novacrypt facility called CySec Station, and a Virodyne research station called Lab-01.
Felix’s data vault heist took place here (Ep 9 flashback), and Thorne’s neo-noir backstory adventure across Hakumei Prefecture with Mara Vex, Brick, and Kano Rix unfolded here as well (Ep 12 flashback).

Appears in: Ep 9, Ep 12

locations/prometheon-station/_prometheon.title: Prometheon Station
locations/prometheon-station/_prometheon.content:
Prometheon Station is a facility tied to Virodyne Labs, first glimpsed by the crew through a portal opened by the Paracausal Bifurcation Array (the Fork) at Exosite 34b on Sibylen. When Voss activated the Fork, a window opened across space showing a massive structure — five interlocking rings arranged like a celestial gyroscope, with a long rod through its center — and strange blue diamond entities became visible nearby. Haleyy screamed and collapsed unconscious as the vision hit (Ep 18).
The station’s name and significance went unconfirmed for many episodes afterward. It resurfaced when the crew infiltrated the secret Virodyne routing station Causeway 3: transit logs there confirmed that Strake’s ship, the Acceptable Loss, had delivered the captured Voss to Prometheon Station (Ep 28) — the first hard confirmation of her location since her capture. A deeper layer of the same records showed that the Omnitek data vault, carrying Petey’s digitized consciousness, had also been routed toward Prometheon Station years earlier and never returned. The crew obtained the drill path to Prometheon Station from Causeway 3’s database before fleeing under pursuit (Ep 29).
As of the crew’s escape from Causeway 3, Prometheon Station remains unreached — a destination now confirmed, but not yet explored.

Appears in: Ep 18, Ep 28, Ep 29

locations/scrapjacks/_scrapjacks.title: Scrapjacks
locations/scrapjacks/_scrapjacks.content:
Scrap Jack’s Refueling and Grub is an interstellar truck stop and fuel depot in the Anagris system, orbiting near the desert world Pare. It has ten landing pads and serves as a waypoint for long-haul spacers, run by Yana 7 with a station AI named Buddy. Scrapjacks is actually a spaceship — it has its own spike drive, though incredibly expensive to operate, letting it relocate if needed.
Scrapjacks used to exist in the inner system closer to Polyphn. As more way stations and corporate-backed operations moved into the sector, independent stops like Scrapjacks couldn’t compete, and it was cheaper to activate the spike drive and relocate than to fight — pushed further and further out over the years. Now it survives by catering to long-haulers, asteroid miners, and ice haulers bringing resources back to the inner systems.
The station enforces a strict no-weapons policy with scanning at the airlock, key-card access for dorms and showers, and just six security staff armed with only batons. It’s currently nowhere near capacity, too far out on the fringes to draw much traffic.
The crew stopped here for fuel and found the station taken over by fifteen Void Cultists (Ep 10-11), who activated a void ansible that tore a rift in spacetime. With their weapons left behind per station policy, the crew had to retrieve them, save hostages, and stop the ritual. During the ordeal, Haleyy was touched by a void tendril and had a vision of surgeons and a worm-like machine, and station security officer Dan Grand was found in crew storage, corrupted and muttering void hymns — the first major appearance of the corrupted state known as Unhallowed. After the crew defeated the cultists, the station’s mechanics fixed The Scapegoat for free.

Appears in: Ep 10, Ep 11

locations/sector-map.title: Sector Overview
locations/sector-map.content:
The sector is mostly split up and owned by a variety of corporations, with fairly defined boundaries in space serving as borders. Three major corporations own most of everything, but pockets of space, individual worlds, stations, and moons remain independent or controlled by smaller factions.
Known systems and worlds include the Schroeter system’s Camiri 4 (gang territory, and the campaign’s starting location); the Revarmi Trita system’s Wafisa (a dead-feeling megacity rich in alien artifacts), Blackharbor (a coastal settlement ruled by the Guardians of the Great Work), Port Ascension (an empty spaceport), and Mistretta 4 (Voss’s Omnitek base); the Lebima system’s Polyphn (a night world and Omnitek headquarters); the Shepherd system’s Sibylen (site of major alien ruins) and its port city The Spigot; the Anagris system’s Scrapjacks (a fuel depot and site of a cultist attack) and the nearby world of Pare; and the Thraxis system’s Ventos (jungle world and site of the Red Rice Wars).
The crew’s route across Season 1 ran from Camiri 4 to Wafisa, to Blackharbor and back to Wafisa, then to Scrapjacks, to Sibylen and The Spigot, and onward toward further destinations.
Alien artifacts move along a trade route from Wafisa through Polyphn to Zephryss III, home of the Draxus Goods trading company.

Appears in: Ep 1-29

locations/sibylen/exosite-34b.title: Exosite 34b
locations/sibylen/exosite-34b.content:
Exosite 34b is an alien quarantine building discovered by Vera Corbin, buried under the sands of Sibylen and long since abandoned. The structure is built on an external skeleton of metal with interiors constructed entirely of nanofluid. Walls are roughly six inches thick and hard as concrete; ceilings run fifteen feet high with oval doorways about three feet wide and ten feet tall. The entrance is a steel door embedded in a dune, marked with a band of sweeping tendril-like alien writing, surrounded by a one-acre dig site of colored flags, steel ladders, and crates.
The upper floor holds a chamber of large goo vats and a “pool room” containing a submersible “digital ocean” — a local alien network, like a LAN — as well as an annihilation bot, a multi-armed defensive machine the crew destroyed. A sublevel below holds a round “nautilus” room with a spiral ridge and a ceiling-mounted track system connecting to the vats above, the Fork Chamber containing the Paracausal Bifurcation Array (known as the Fork, a three-tined black metal pylon), and a surgical room where two “chainsaw” surgical spider-bots once operated on patients. A goo-powered transparent tube leads out through the wall on the sublevel, filling with goo over about two hours to serve as an escape route.
The crew arrived with Vera Corbin and explored the upper level (Ep 14-16); Felix was submerged in the nanofluid (Ep 15) and the crew fought the annihilation bot (Ep 16). They navigated the goo shaft and solved the nautilus room puzzle to reach the surgical chamber, encountering the chainsaw med-bots (Ep 17), which they then defeated — Robert riding one, Felix manipulating the ceiling via the goo interface, and Haleyy destroying one with a laser rifle. Dr. Elara Voss then activated the Fork using accumulated nanofluid, opening a portal that showed a distant structure — five interlocking rings arranged like a celestial gyroscope — with strange blue diamond entities visible nearby. Felix and Voss sensed an alien presence through the goo interface, and Haleyy screamed and collapsed unconscious; Robert hinted at prior contact with similar alien tech on Ventos (Ep 18).
Later, a Nexus Trading crew led by Rynn Kade took control of the sublevel and wired three captives to the Fork in a second attempt to replicate the earlier merge (Ep 21-23). When the crew descended to retrieve them, a Nexus psionicist scanned the group before Robert killed him mid-monologue, and Rynn Kade shot Thorne through the chest in a sucker punch that left him moments from death. While the crew argued over whether disconnecting the captives would kill them or save them, the Fork completed its process, and the three captives were fully merged. Haleyy activated a biosionic healing touch for the first time, saving Thorne’s life (Ep 24).
The facility had originally housed infected aliens submerged in their own nanofluid, connected to a virtual network as they slowly died to a plague — the lower floor’s surgical system was used to move patients from the vats for care, experimentation, and autopsy in increasingly desperate attempts to find a cure.

Appears in: Ep 14, Ep 15, Ep 16, Ep 17, Ep 18, Ep 21, Ep 22, Ep 23, Ep 24

locations/sibylen/the-gloam-trenches.title: The Gloam Trenches
locations/sibylen/the-gloam-trenches.content:
The Gloam Trenches are jagged canyons that split the surface of Sibylen like scars, up to a kilometer deep — the most famous and significant archaeological feature on the planet, known to explorers across the sector and the site of most xenoarchaeological expeditions there. The ruins within are labyrinths of black stone etched with pulsating lines of silvery metal that defy analysis. The sites are known to shift mysteriously — mapping efforts are notoriously unreliable, as tunnels sometimes appear to move or reconfigure between visits.

Appears in: Ep 14

locations/sibylen/the-spigot/helium-dock.title: Helium Docks
locations/sibylen/the-spigot/helium-dock.content:
The Helium Docks are a loading zone on the outskirts of The Spigot on Sibylen, between the town and the helium-3 mines — a collection of landing platforms circled with wire fencing and a single wide opening barred by a security arm and card sensor. Three automated turrets target via infrared sentry cameras, and a speaker shouts warnings at anyone accessing the landing zone without proper clearance. Autonomous cargo shipments arrive at 3am; the ship lands, bots unload it within thirty minutes, and it departs, with no human personnel present.
The crew needed a black-market ownership module and staged a heist during the 3am autonomous shipment. A Viktor Strake clone attacked with drones during the raid, and Dr. Iso fought alongside the crew with her shotgun (Ep 27). The warehouse yielded a motorcycle, pharmaceuticals, and roughly 2,500 credits worth of goods.

Appears in: Ep 27

locations/sibylen/the-spigot/iso's-shop.title: Iso's Shop
locations/sibylen/the-spigot/iso's-shop.content:
Iso’s Shop was Dr. Iso’s clinic and black market shop in The Spigot on Sibylen — a single-story concrete building in a less-traveled part of town, a leaky air unit staining the wall with rust. Inside, it was narrow but long, cluttered floor to ceiling with medical equipment, vials, potions, and disconnected electronics, with a long blue curtain across the back.
Haleyy led the crew here so Iso could scan her brain, revealing crystalline structures growing inside it (Ep 25). A Robert-line clone was later found dead outside the shop, killed by Iso’s security turret, and the shop itself was burned down — arson tied to Strake’s forces. Iso joined the crew after losing her shop (Ep 27).

Appears in: Ep 25, Ep 27

locations/sibylen/the-spigot/the-vent.title: The Vent
locations/sibylen/the-spigot/the-vent.content:
The Vent is a local bar in The Spigot on Sibylen — a quiet room of weary miners eating lunch or having a drink, with a blue-collar atmosphere.
Dr. Iso brought the crew here to find mechanic Peter Haslow, who was drinking at the bar. Thorne sat beside him under cover and paid for intel on an upcoming black-market shipment. A grenade was then thrown through the window; Robert dove on it and tossed it behind the bar, but the bartender was killed in the blast. Iso pursued the attacker into an alley but lost him, and the bar was left partially destroyed, gas line igniting, as people evacuated (Ep 25).

Appears in: Ep 25

locations/sibylen/the-spigot/_the-spigot.title: The Spigot
locations/sibylen/the-spigot/_the-spigot.content:
The Spigot, also known as Delta-7, is the port city on Sibylen — a sprawling town that grew organically into a twisting maze of sun-baked streets and concrete modular apartments, centered on a refueling tower stretching from the surface to low orbit. As the poet Cassius put it: “The Spigot is the rusty throat of the innerbelt, ever swallowing the dreams of silver men.” It’s known for insatiable blue-collar labor, with helium-3 mining fields nearby worked by conveyor bots.
Sub-locations include The Vent, a local bar; Iso’s Shop (destroyed), Dr. Iso’s former clinic and black market shop; the Helium Docks, a loading zone between town and the mines; and the spaceport admin office.
The crew brought their damaged ship here for repairs (Ep 25). Haleyy led them to Dr. Iso’s shop, where Iso scanned her and confirmed crystalline microstructures growing in her frontal lobe. Iso then led the crew to The Vent to identify mechanic Peter Haslow as a source of intel on black-market ownership modules; Thorne got the details of an upcoming shipment from him, but a grenade thrown through the bar’s window killed the bartender before Robert could dispose of it outside. The crew suspected Viktor Strake had sent the attacker.
Investigating further, Felix hacked the Spigot’s camera network and traced the attacker to a docked Omnitech transport at the spaceport. Thorne infiltrated the spaceport admin office to route camera access back to Felix, and the crew breached the ship to find a second Robert-line clone, designated DT7X, who confirmed he’d tracked the Scapegoat using leftover Omnitech admin codes (Ep 26). Iso’s shop was later found bombed, with another Robert-line clone dead inside, and Iso officially joined the crew after losing her shop. The crew then raided the Helium Docks for the ownership module shipment (Ep 27).

Appears in: Ep 25, Ep 26, Ep 27

locations/sibylen/_sibylen.title: Sibylen
locations/sibylen/_sibylen.content:
Sibylen is infamous across the sector for the sprawling ruins of an ancient alien species buried beneath its sands and cliffs — the most significant xenoarchaeological site in the sector. From space it appears as a dull gray ball streaked with black, naked and exposed with no cloud cover, with lines of cargo ships queuing in orbit to fuel. Despite appearing dead from orbit, the surface has birdsong, insects, and other life.
The planet orbits Shepherd, an F-type white dwarf, giving its skies a permanent amber hue. Atmosphere is thin but breathable, gravity is low-normal, and the terrain is vast bone-white desert, wind-scoured plateaus, and labyrinthine canyons. Population is under 500,000, almost entirely researchers and support staff. The ruins themselves are labyrinths of black stone etched with pulsating lines of silvery metal.
Before the alien discoveries, Sibylen functioned as essentially a planet-sized gas station — a fuel stop for long-haul truckers. The planet’s weak magnetosphere and thin atmosphere let stellar winds hammer the surface, embedding Helium-3 directly into the sand, so miners simply rake it from the dunes rather than scooping it from space. The port city, The Spigot, sits on one side of the planet; the He-3 strip mines are on the other, with huge conveyors cutting through dunes and miners in sealed suits fighting constant sandstorms. The alien dig sites, including The Gloam Trenches, sit on the far side from the port, where the original artifacts were found roughly seven years ago.
A massive fuel tower reaches from the surface to orbit, with ships queuing alongside it to refuel — the source of the orbital queue visible from space. The General Store, an orbital station beside the queue, lets truckers place supply orders ahead of time for pickup during the fueling queue. Exo-Net access is normally free, but on Sibylen the corporations seized control of it and charge steep rates, so a free local-only exo site sprang up for the general population.
Surface locations include The Spigot, Exosite 34b (an alien quarantine building), The Gloam Trenches, and the He-3 mining fields. Laicar Research, led by Vera Corbin, maintains a presence here, and Void Cultists and multiple corporations — including Virodyne Labs and Novacrypt Solutions — have taken interest as well.
The crew arrived and met Vera Corbin, exploring the exosite (Ep 14). The Fork was activated (Ep 18), revealing a distant structure across space and alien entities that caused Haleyy to collapse. Viktor Strake later captured the crew, and an auction over the exosite was attacked by Void Cultists, during which The Concordant was created through “the Joining” and Haleyy discovered a healing touch (Ep 21). The crew fled to The Spigot for repairs afterward (Ep 22).

Appears in: Ep 14, Ep 15, Ep 16, Ep 17, Ep 18, Ep 21, Ep 22, Ep 23, Ep 24

locations/the-orbital-data-vault.title: The Orbital Data Vault
locations/the-orbital-data-vault.content:
The Orbital Data Vault is a massive three-story pyramid, an Omnitech facility used for data storage and other purposes. It originally drifted in orbit above Polyphn. Its exterior is a rotating pyramid crisscrossed with rail tracks for maintenance drones, reinforced docking ports, security nodes, and weaponized flying drones with glowing red eyes. The airlock is barely large enough for three or four people, and a half-android receptionist impaled on a rod performs voice-print analysis as the facility’s most common first line of security. A spinning corridor of rotating laser beams serves as a further security measure, leading to an inner data room with telescopic arms, monitors, and cables where Victor Saren appears as a digital blue face.
Years ago, Felix Champlin assembled a crew — his brother Petey Champlin, cat burglar Nyx Verhoeven, and gunslinger Jett Harlow — to break in (Ep 9 flashback). They discovered the truth: Omnitech had been digitizing prisoner consciousnesses and killing their bodies, and Petey’s consciousness had been extracted and trapped in the servers. The vault was “in migratory mode,” about to relocate, during the heist, which explained its unusually heavy security that night. Felix escaped but burned his identity in the process, and the vault was later relocated far from any known drill paths. Felix’s long-term goal has been to kill Victor Saren and rescue Petey’s digitized consciousness — part of why he joined Dr. Voss’s mission was that the signal coordinates she was chasing were near the vault’s new location.
By the crew’s investigation of the Causeway 3 routing station, historical transit records confirmed that the Orbital Data Vault, with Petey aboard, had transited through Causeway 3 years earlier bound for Prometheon Station — and never returned (Ep 29).

Appears in: Ep 9, Ep 29

locations/ventos/_ventos.title: Ventos
locations/ventos/_ventos.content:
Ventos is a planet in the Thraxis system with inhospitable jungles, extremely hot and humid — the system’s breadbasket despite the harsh terrain. Haleyy grew up on Vigrid, another planet in the same system.
Ventos was the site of the Red Rice Wars, a famine-driven war triggered by an invasive offworld insect that destroyed most food production. Rice was resistant, making it the staple crop, but there wasn’t enough to go around. The government — a so-called meritocracy predicated on “good ideas” but in reality an oligarchy of ancestral privilege — hoarded food stores. A rebellion ignited but was ultimately crushed with Omnitek Holdings military backing, and the oligarchy remains in power.
Dense jungle on Ventos hides a cave system containing an alien structure holding a three-tined fork — the same type of alien artifact found at the Sibylen exosite. “Haley” (with one Y) — before she became Haleyy — was stationed here on loan from Omnitek to defend the oligarchy, defected to help the rebels, and was captured. A squadron was sent to extract her from the oligarchy’s elite captivity in the cave system; inside, the alien fork struck her with energy, her eyes turning green and hair singeing. The squad escaped on stolen motorcycles through the jungle, but an anti-air mech shot down their extraction helicopter, killing several squadmates. Haley died from her crash injuries and was later revived in the morgue with alien-enhanced healing, waking with amnesia as “Haleyy” (Ep 19 flashback).

Appears in: Ep 19

locations/wafisa/17-millbrook-lane.title: 17 Millbrook Lane
locations/wafisa/17-millbrook-lane.content:
17 Millbrook Lane is the residence of the Harrow family on Wafisa. The crew found it by following instructions left by Michael Harrow on his laptop at the Glendale Hotel — an unsent email draft with the subject line “if someone finds this go to 17 Millbrook Lane” and body text reading “there’s a book in the bottom drawer.”
Following the instructions, the crew found the Lokipon Cards and the Harrow Family Cookbook here. The cookbook is a red notebook spanning three generations, with roughly a hundred blank pages in the back suggesting it may be more than just recipes.

Appears in: Ep 5, Ep 6

locations/wafisa/blackharbor/the-docks.title: The Docks (Blackharbor)
locations/wafisa/blackharbor/the-docks.content:
The Docks are the heart of Blackharbor’s industry on Wafisa — aquatic creature traps, fishing boats, and seaweed farms, all tightly controlled by the Guardians of the Great Work, who levy high taxes on every haul. Smuggling rings operate in secret here, slipping extra fish to starving families.

Appears in: Ep 7

locations/wafisa/blackharbor/the-great-m.title: The Great Market
locations/wafisa/blackharbor/the-great-m.content:
The Great Market is an open-air market in Blackharbor on Wafisa where dried fish, livestock, black-market tech, and handmade goods are traded under the watchful eye of Guardian patrols. Hidden beneath the stalls and in basements, rebel messengers and traders whisper of resistance.

Appears in: Ep 7

locations/wafisa/blackharbor/the-guardia.title: The Guardian Compound
locations/wafisa/blackharbor/the-guardia.content:
The Guardian Compound is the military base of the Guardians of the Great Work in Blackharbor on Wafisa — half a mile square, a fortress of concrete and steel surrounded by walls, watchtowers, and automated turrets. Inside, well-fed officers plan the next round of taxation, conscription, and suppression.

Appears in: Ep 7

locations/wafisa/blackharbor/the-iron-ch.title: The Iron Chapel
locations/wafisa/blackharbor/the-iron-ch.content:
The Iron Chapel is a former pre-collapse church in Blackharbor on Wafisa, now serving as a makeshift hospital, shelter, and rebel meeting place. It’s run by Brother Edric. The Guardians of the Great Work tolerate its existence, but rumors persist that the priest is aiding the resistance.

Appears in: Ep 7

locations/wafisa/blackharbor/the-militar.title: The Military Airfield
locations/wafisa/blackharbor/the-militar.content:
The Military Airfield sits on the northern edge of Blackharbor on Wafisa, abutting the green ocean. Once much larger, it’s now bombed out to a quarter of its original size, with three active landing strips remaining and roughly 2,500 Guardian soldiers stationed there.
The Scapegoat was taken here after being stolen, and the crew reclaimed their ship from the airfield in Ep 7, with Viktor Strake sending soldiers to trace them here.

Appears in: Ep 7

locations/wafisa/blackharbor/the-outer-f.title: The Outer Farms
locations/wafisa/blackharbor/the-outer-f.content:
The Outer Farms are struggling livestock ranches and hydroponic greenhouses on the outskirts of Blackharbor on Wafisa. The Guardians of the Great Work seize the best crops, and some residents secretly raise extra animals in underground pens to hide them from Guardian inspections.

Appears in: Ep 7

locations/wafisa/blackharbor/the-rust-ya.title: The Rust Yards
locations/wafisa/blackharbor/the-rust-ya.content:
The Rust Yards are a sprawling junkyard in Blackharbor on Wafisa where scavengers tear apart pre-collapse machines to extract anything useful. The Guardians of the Great Work claim all fuel, batteries, and salvageable power sources, leaving only scraps for the people.
The auxiliary lot, a cleared-out section of the yards, is where a Draxus Goods ship is currently parked — a two-person team runs it along its trade routes for Nexus Trading.

Appears in: Ep 7

locations/wafisa/blackharbor/_blackharbo.title: Blackharbor
locations/wafisa/blackharbor/_blackharbo.content:
Blackharbor is a coastal settlement on Wafisa, north of the megacity, struggling under the rule of the Guardians of the Great Work. It’s home to fisherfolk, scavengers, and farmers living in squalor while the military extracts wealth and resources to fund their impossible “Great Work.” The population is roughly 2,500 civilians, alongside a Guardian garrison of about 2,500 soldiers at the airfield.
Outside Blackharbor’s walls lie fields of purple flowers, grown as an industry and shipped off-world for narcotics and medication, alongside a thriving seaside fishing community. Haleyy set the fields on fire in Ep 7 as a distraction during the crew’s escape.
The settlement is divided into districts: the fishing quarter of The Docks, the open-air The Great Market, the scavenging grounds of The Rust Yards, the ranches and greenhouses of The Outer Farms, the hospital-shelter of The Iron Chapel, the fortress of The Guardian Compound, and The Military Airfield, where The Scapegoat was held after being confiscated.
Blackharbor trades alien artifacts when available, selling them to Draxus Goods via a route running from Wafisa through Polyphn to Zephryss III. The crew’s ship was held at the Military Airfield until they reclaimed it, with Viktor Strake sending soldiers to trace them there (Ep 7).

Appears in: Ep 7

locations/wafisa/glendale-hotel.title: Glendale Hotel
locations/wafisa/glendale-hotel.content:
The Glendale Hotel is a seven-story hotel on Wafisa that has been completely ransacked. On the fourth floor, the crew found a barricaded room containing two dead bodies — Michael and Claire Harrow. Video, notes, and other information found here led the crew to 17 Millbrook Lane and Millbrook Storage.

Appears in: Ep 5

locations/wafisa/millbrook-storage.title: Millbrook Storage
locations/wafisa/millbrook-storage.content:
Millbrook Storage is a ransacked storage facility on Wafisa, near the Harrow residence.
