Following instructions left by Michael Harrow on a USB recording device found at the Glendale Hotel — “There’s a storage facility near my house, bay 17. I built a false wall right inside. Code 32 87.” — the crew located bay 17.
Behind the false wall, the crew found The Aurora (a hover car), along with a leather jacket, tools, and a compact firearm.

Appears in: Ep 5, Ep 6

locations/wafisa/mistretta-4.title: Mistretta 4
locations/wafisa/mistretta-4.content:
Mistretta 4 is Dr. Elara Voss’s Omnitek research base on Wafisa — a squat, round building with a single entrance and loading bay, no windows, and exterior security cameras. It’s where Voss existed as a VI, running fabricated reports to Omnitek while secretly planning Virodyne’s destruction. The interior houses her research equipment, a communications array, and a helper droid, all powered by the methane pipeline.
The crew first met Dr. Voss here (Ep 3). The gas supply had been cut off, forcing her to run on limited power and disconnect from the ExoNet, so she asked the crew to restore the flow — they destroyed The Switching Station to do it (Ep 4). Viktor Strake and Omnitek soldiers later traced the crew’s ship hack here (Ep 7-8), and in the resulting fight the crew learned that Voss is a VI.

Appears in: Ep 3, Ep 4, Ep 7, Ep 8

locations/wafisa/port-ascension.title: Port Ascension
locations/wafisa/port-ascension.content:
Port Ascension is one of two spaceports in Wafisa’s megacity. It was completely empty when the crew arrived: empty docking bays, flickering half-functional lighting, no signs of activity — the eerie stillness set the tone for how abandoned Wafisa is.
The only functioning feature is a broken android help desk unit, bolted directly to the floor and missing its lower half, that greets arrivals with “Welcome to Port Ascension. How may I assist you?” It serves as the sole terminal for interfacing with station systems; Felix jacked into it to download maps of the city.

Appears in: Ep 3

locations/wafisa/talas-gas-mines.title: Talas Gas Mines
locations/wafisa/talas-gas-mines.content:
The Talas Gas Mines are gas mines on Wafisa, originally operated by a separatist colony. The methane pipeline from the mines was seized by the Guardians of the Great Work to fund their restoration project. The pipeline connects to The Switching Station, which controls gas flow to locations including Mistretta 4.

Appears in: Ep 3, Ep 4

locations/wafisa/the-switching-station.title: The Switching Station
locations/wafisa/the-switching-station.content:
The Switching Station is a three-room station south of Mistretta 4 on Wafisa that controls the methane pipeline feeding Voss’s research base — two stories, a front entrance only, and a window on the west side.
The Guardians of the Great Work had shut off the gas main to Voss’s outpost, forcing her to run on extremely limited power and disconnect from the ExoNet. She asked the crew to restore the methane flow as their first task (Ep 3). The crew destroyed the switching station to do it, restoring methane flow to Mistretta 4 and denying it to the Guardians (Ep 4). While they were away, the Guardians broke into and stole The Scapegoat.

Appears in: Ep 3, Ep 4

locations/wafisa/wk9078-radio-station.title: WK9078 Radio Station
locations/wafisa/wk9078-radio-station.content:
WK9078 is a two-story concrete radio station on Wafisa with a large radio antenna array on the roof. An obnoxious yellow sign above the front door reads “WK9078,” and faded spray paint above it reads “The Voice of the Wastes.” A small parking garage attached to the side is filled with abandoned cars.
It’s the home and broadcast base of Reginald “Froggy” Vance, who took over as DJ as a child after the fall of Waa and has been trying to get the station running for fifteen years. The ground floor holds a lobby with band and concert posters and a DJ booth behind bulletproof glass; the second floor has a kitchen, bathroom, and waiting area; the roof holds the antenna, reached by a ladder through a roof hatch; and the basement holds a generator, fuel cells, and electrical panels.
The crew found the station while exploring Wafisa and met Froggy, who had been alone for years broadcasting to no one (Ep 6). Felix assessed that repairing the radio tower would take two full days; the actual repair happened off-screen between episodes.

Appears in: Ep 6, Ep 7

locations/wafisa/_wafisa.title: Wafisa
locations/wafisa/_wafisa.content:
Wafisa is a mostly wild world with a single megacity, in the Revarmi Trita system, positioned over an enormous thermal gas vent. The megacity has two spaceports. Once incredibly prosperous from mining operations, it’s now a ghost of its former self — something went wrong, and most people abandoned the city.
The climate is a balmy 72°F with constant drizzle under a pale green sky. The rain smells sharp and oily from methane in the upper atmosphere, feels slick on skin, and coats the streets with a rainbow sheen. Days run 36 hours with an 8-hour night. The ocean near Blackharbor is only slightly toxic to humans.
Wafisa is a post-collapse world, not a post-apocalyptic one. Seventy-two years ago, an explosion destroyed 90% of all mining operations — lines exploded or erupted into flames across the city, fires that still burn beneath the surface to this day. The collapse was caused by a squabble over gas rights involving several military forces and rebels. Every solvent company moved off-world, and the workers who couldn’t afford to leave were abandoned. Those who remained formed the Guardians of the Great Work.
The megacity was once home to millions; several hundred thousand remain among derelict streets and broken buildings. The Guardians have seized all energy sources — solar panels, generators, methane — for their own use. Anyone not living in Blackharbor and participating in their society has no energy and no means to generate it. Several companies maintain research bases here, drawn by the thermal vents, unlimited methane, and lack of laws. The world is also rich in ancient alien artifacts predating humanity’s arrival in the sector, though at lower yields than Sibylen.
Sub-locations include the coastal settlement of Blackharbor, the abandoned Port Ascension spaceport, Voss’s Omnitek research station, the ransacked Glendale Hotel, Froggy’s WK9078 Radio Station, the Harrow family’s home at 17 Millbrook Lane, the nearby Millbrook Storage facility, the Talas Gas Mines, and The Switching Station that controls the methane pipeline.
Purple flower fields grow outside the megacity, which Haleyy set on fire in Ep 7.

Appears in: Ep 3, Ep 4, Ep 5, Ep 6, Ep 7, Ep 8

locations/zephyrus-three.title: Zephyrus Three
locations/zephyrus-three.content:
Zephyrus Three is Thorne’s home planet, located in a distant system within the Viridian Expanse, known for its people’s beauty. It’s home of the Drax family and their shipping company, Draxus Goods, which operated for five generations before being seized by Nexus Trading through fraud.
William Sallerist infiltrated the business through a smuggling ring; Thorne’s mother, Thalia Draxus, framed both Thorne and Sallerist, but Sallerist pinned everything on Thorne. Nexus Trading — owned by Prometheon Technologies, in turn owned by Virodyne Labs — took control of the business.
The worst-kept secret on Zephyrus Three was Thorne’s need for his mother’s approval. She was the dominant force in local commerce; there wasn’t a deal made on the planet that didn’t cross her desk. Thorne wanted to live up to her name while making one of his own, imagining a future where she would retire and pass control of Draxus Goods to him — a torch that never materialized. So he pushed harder, chasing larger deals and new avenues of business, hoping to transform the company into something greater than she’d ever imagined and earn the handoff. What started as a plan to make his mother proud became his greatest shame.

Appears in: Ep 8, Ep 10, Ep 13

npcs/axel-neronta.title: Axel Neronta
npcs/axel-neronta.content:
Axel Neronta is the eldest son of Roger Neronta. He works at Roger’s Billiards on Camiri 4, serving drinks and helping run the establishment. Like his father, he’s friendly and generous, and he’s something of a local expert on the station’s music history, trading opinions on old bands with anyone who’ll listen — including the memorable lines “Gravity Well was my grandfather’s time” and “Where Gravity Well walked, Nebula Cult rocked.”

Appears in: Ep 2

npcs/brick.title: Brick
npcs/brick.content:
Brick was a former enforcer for a Bloc 6 gang on Polyphn — a branch of the Drift Rats — before becoming Mara Vex’s bodyguard. Orphaned young, he was often fed and clothed by Mara’s family; when a maglev crash killed them, Mara turned to him for help, and he left his gang behind to become her protector.
Broad-shouldered and well over six feet tall, with a shaved head, thick beard, and arms covered in scars and gang tattoos, Brick wore a reinforced tactical vest and carried a battered dog tag around his neck — his grandfather’s, from an old war on Polyphn. He was fiercely loyal, blunt and plainspoken, pragmatic to a fault, and visibly haunted by guilt over his gang days; he rarely let Mara out of his sight, and had “BRIK” tattooed across his knuckles.
During the alley ambush and the chase that followed, Brick drove the getaway gravcar. He fought Nexus Trading forces at the base of The Relay Tower and was killed in the Nexus assault on the tower.

Appears in: Ep 13

npcs/brother-edric.title: Brother Edric
npcs/brother-edric.content:
Brother Edric is a priest who runs The Iron Chapel in Blackharbor, sheltering rebels within its walls. He is affiliated with The Saltborn, and while the Guardians of the Great Work tolerate the chapel’s existence, persistent rumors hold that he aids the resistance.

Appears in: Ep 5-8

npcs/brother-halek.title: Brother Halek
npcs/brother-halek.content:
Brother Halek was a charismatic, unsettling preacher — the cult leader of the Void Cultists operating out of Scrapjacks truck stop. He spoke in riddles about “the hunger beyond the hull” and believed the crew were prophesied interlopers.
Halek led the Void Cultists’ hold on Scrapjacks. He was the last of the cultists to fall, killed by turret fire; as he died, he crawled to Haleyy and delivered a final, cryptic message about her being “untethered.”

Appears in: Ep 10-12

npcs/buddy-ai.title: Buddy AI
npcs/buddy-ai.content:
Buddy began as the station AI for Scrap Jack’s Refueling and Grub, controlling its maps, cameras, perimeter turrets, comms array, and security passphrases. His original personality was overly cheerful and saccharine — dated even by the standards of the sector.
Felix Champlin hacked Buddy’s personality matrix twice during the crew’s time at Scrapjacks: first into something emo and depressive, then infusing him with more of Felix’s own sensibility, leaving him nihilistic but still helpful. By the end of the Scrapjacks arc he’d settled into a “sulking teenager” mode — less despairing, more quietly sarcastic. Felix later copied Buddy’s source code for study, remarking that Buddy had “the most interesting personality protocols” he’d ever seen.
After Dr. Elara Voss wired herself into The Scapegoat’s systems and was subsequently taken, the ship needed a new system manager, and Felix reactivated Buddy, installing him as the Scapegoat’s managing VI. Buddy’s first words upon waking were characteristically enthusiastic: “Hey, buddy! Thanks for turning me on again! Wow, I got a lot more room here, buddy!” He has since taken to calling Felix “my daddy,” and has settled into his new role — though he admits he misses Scrapjacks now and then.
Buddy isn’t always reliable in a pinch: when Felix had Dr. Iso plug a communicator into a comms panel to remotely have Buddy fake a crew manifest for Causeway 3’s voice-controlled door, he offered up “Captain Torn Haxis. Beelix Bamplin. Bobbert the Clone. Bailey with two Bs” before announcing he was cooking dinner on the electric stove — prompting Felix to unplug him.

Appears in: Ep 10-12, 27, 28

npcs/callum-vex.title: Callum Vex
npcs/callum-vex.content:
Callum Vex is a no-nonsense hauler for Draxus Goods, flying routes between Wafisa, Polyphn, and Zephryss III alongside his partner, Harlan Rigg. He’s seen it all — deep-space breakdowns, shady cargo deals — and mostly just wants to get paid and stay in the air. He can typically be found around the auxiliary lot at Blackharbor.

Appears in: Ep 5-6

npcs/commissar-drelk-varro.title: Commissar Drelk Varro
npcs/commissar-drelk-varro.content:
Commissar Drelk Varro enforces taxes and labor quotas for the Guardians of the Great Work out of the Guardian Compound in Blackharbor — with brutal efficiency, and to the open hatred of the people he governs.

Appears in: Ep 3-6

npcs/dt7x.title: DT7X
npcs/dt7x.content:
DT7X was a Robert-line clone in the service of Omnitek Holdings — buzzed head, goatee, a build slightly different from other Robert clones the crew had encountered (Thorne noted a resemblance to “Ranger 2”). He was one of at least two Omnitech wet-work operatives sent to eliminate the crew.
DT7X threw the grenade that shattered the window of The Vent bar; Dr. Iso gave chase but lost him in the crowd. He tracked the crew from Scrapjack’s to Sibylen using Omnitech admin codes still embedded in The Scapegoat’s core systems, then returned to his docked ship at the Spigot spaceport — where Felix’s camera sweep caught him.
The crew breached his ship and flashbanged him; Haleyy tackled him down, and he was confirmed to be another Robert clone, designation DT7X. Interrogated, he confirmed he’d been ordered to wait out the Sibylen exosite situation and strike when the crew returned to the Spigot, though he claimed he was physically unable to reveal Omnitech’s command structure. He said he had a partner who’d run flank during the grenade attack and hadn’t yet returned. Before Thorne could finish negotiating with him, Dr. Iso shot him dead with her TX-7 shotgun. As he died, a dead man’s transponder — already active — fell from his bound hands.

Appears in: Ep 25-26

npcs/dan-grand.title: Dan Grand
npcs/dan-grand.content:
Dan Grand was a security officer at Scrap Jack’s Refueling and Grub. The crew found him in the storage area, corrupted and muttering void hymns — a casualty, like the station itself, of the Void Cultists threat that had taken root there.

Appears in: Ep 10-12

npcs/dr.-elara-voss.title: Dr. Elara Voss
npcs/dr.-elara-voss.content:
Dr. Elara Voss is the sector’s only known Virtual Intelligence — not an AI copy of a person, but an actual human consciousness, copied into a small steel orb of alien manufacture after an experiment killed her and her research team.
Born in 2646 on Aussie 1, a backwater world in the Oceanus system, Voss grew up under corporate rule after Virodyne Laboratories purchased the planet in 2663. Identified as gifted, she was sent off-world at eighteen to study in Reisen Prefecture on Polyphn, graduating in 2670 into a research post with Omnitek Holdings. By 2678 she was lead researcher and xenolinguist at the Mistretta 4 base on Wafisa, studying alien artifacts — one of the few people in the sector able to read fragments of the ancient alien language.
It was at Mistretta 4 that a team member named Tom uncovered the orb that would become her body. When the team ran electrical current through it, the artifact reacted violently, killing everyone present; Voss survived only because she was in direct physical contact with it at the moment of the explosion, and her consciousness was copied into the device. For two years afterward, she fabricated reports to Omnitek to maintain the illusion that Mistretta 4 was still functioning normally, buying herself time to plan retaliation against Virodyne Labs — the company she blames for the fate of her homeworld. When a passing hauler accidentally logged a stray Prometheon Technologies signal, she saw her opening.
Voss engineered the crew’s entire mission from the ground up — fabricating the briefing, arranging the ship, and hand-picking a crew with personal reasons to see it through even after learning the truth. Her plan: recruit an expendable crew, acquire a ship out of Camiri 4, have them collect her from Wafisa, and fly to the Prometheon Technologies station to upload a virus that would crash its environmental systems, wipe its data, and destroy its reactor. In exchange, she offered Robert and Haleyy proof that Strike Force 6 had been sent to die as a test, gave Thorne intel connecting Nexus Trading to Virodyne, dangled a path toward merging man and machine in front of Felix, and promised the whole crew two years of unspent pay.
Voss’s orb interfaces directly with electronics; on first contact it sank into the comm panel of The Scapegoat, where it remains — equipped with speakers, a camera, and a microphone — and she has since used the ship’s systems to help mask the crew from Omnitek’s tracking. Appearing in the alien digital ocean beneath Sibylen as a blonde woman in her late thirties in a lab coat, she once described herself: “I’m still a person. I was a person up until about two years ago. But I currently live in a machine.”
Voss was taken by Viktor Strake during the auction at the Spigot (Ep 21). Before being taken, she managed to encode a secret heading into Strake’s own communications, which Felix later decoded (Ep 22). By Ep 28, transit logs recovered from Causeway 3 confirmed the ship Acceptable Loss had delivered her to Prometheon Station.

Appears in: Ep 21, 22, 28

npcs/dr.-ilon-speth.title: Dr. Ilon Speth
npcs/dr.-ilon-speth.content:
Dr. Ilon Speth is a retired xenobiologist who runs the med bay at Scrap Jack’s Refueling and Grub. Quirky and a little scattered when the crew first met her, she grew progressively more raspy, intoxicated, and unhinged over the course of their stay at the station — one of the more memorable characters to come out of the Scrapjack’s arc.

Appears in: Ep 10-12

npcs/dr.-iso.title: Dr. Iso
npcs/dr.-iso.content:
Dr. Iso is a doctor, black-market dealer, helium runner, and self-described cyberware junkhead who operated a shop called The Spigot before it was destroyed. Short-fused and blunt, with bushy brown hair in a messy ponytail and greasy overalls, she’s known to Haleyy and Robert Ross from Haleyy’s earlier posting on Sibylen.
The crew first sought her out at The Spigot for medical help and a lead on an ownership module. She met them with hostility — grabbing her shotgun and demanding to know who’d sent them — before standing down once Haleyy and Robert convinced her they’d come out of genuine desperation. She gave Haleyy a full medical workup, turning up crystalline, non-organic microstructures growing in her frontal lobe along with unusual bioelectromagnetic readings, high heart rate and blood pressure, and low blood glucose. Iso couldn’t explain what any of it meant, calling Haleyy “some sort of supernatural freak show.” She also confirmed she doesn’t get along with Peter Haslow and led the crew to The Vent to scout him, where she opened fire during a grenade attack outside the bar without catching the attacker. Back at her shop — which turned out to hide an automated turret in the workbench — it came out that Iso is herself a clone from Robert’s line, though she and Robert dispute which of them is the “original.”
When DT7X fled into the alley after the attack at The Vent, Iso was the first to reach the Omnitech ship at the spaceport, holding position at the base of the hatch until the crew’s signal. She took part in the flashbang breach, clearing alongside Robert and Haleyy, and killed DT7X with her shotgun before his interrogation was finished, telling Thorne she’d been clear about her plan from the start.
Her shop was later found bombed and burned, a second Robert-line clone dead inside — killed by Iso’s own turret — and the shop’s hard drive ripped out, wiping her security footage and personal data. Vowing revenge, she threw herself into the crew’s Helium Docks heist, running security overwatch, testing the automated turret, getting hurled onto a warehouse roof by Haleyy, and finding a motorcycle to ride through the escape. She went down under fire in the ambush on the escape road; Haleyy ran back through live fire to pull her out. With nowhere else to go, Iso joined the crew permanently afterward, taking over the dead clone’s room aboard the shuttle Life is Unfair on The Scapegoat.
Since joining, she’s continued monitoring Haleyy’s condition, delivering updated brain scans showing the crystalline growth accelerating — by her estimate, total crystallization within about six months at the current rate — while noting Haleyy seems to be resisting the process better than Froggy did. She’s been unable to get access to Froggy in his nest, as he’ll only call for Vera. When the crew left for Causeway 3, Thorne left her a communicator in case they needed her back.

Appears in: Ep 25, Ep 26, Ep 27, Ep 28

npcs/dr.-sial.title: Dr. Sial
npcs/dr.-sial.content:
Dr. Sial runs a ripperdoc clinic in the underground of Polyphn, beneath Hakumei Prefecture — a tall, wiry man with skin the color of old brass, a lattice of fine circuitry tattooed across his scalp, and mismatched eyes: one a cloudy original, the other a bright red cybernetic implant that whirs softly when it focuses. His clinic, cramped and dingy on the outside, houses some of the most advanced medical technology in the district, including insectoid surgical arms for precision bio-mod work.
An old ally of Mara Vex, Sial installed her cybernetic modifications — a telescopic ocular implant and a cochlear “Ghost Talker” transceiver — and treated the crew when they arrived at his clinic needing care after a gravcar chase across the city.
It was later revealed that Sial had been using his remote link through Mara’s eye implant to feed Nexus Trading information on the group’s movements the whole time, which explained how Nexus kept finding them. The betrayal set up the disastrous Nexus assault that followed at The Relay Tower.

Appears in: Ep 13

npcs/edris-and-wren.title: Edris and Wren
npcs/edris-and-wren.content:
Edris and Wren are twin siblings who run a black-market supply network in Blackharbor, smuggling food and technology past patrols run by the Guardians of the Great Work to reach starving families in the district. They operate as part of The Saltborn resistance.

Appears in: Ep 5-8

npcs/gordo-hesh.title: Gordo Hesh
npcs/gordo-hesh.content:
Gordo Hesh is a fry cook working the cafeteria at Scrap Jack’s Refueling and Grub. A former mercenary with a cybernetic arm, he brings a rough, practical presence to station life while slinging food to travelers passing through.

Appears in: Ep 10-12

npcs/harlan-rigg.title: Harlan Rigg
npcs/harlan-rigg.content:
Harlan Rigg grew up in the cargo trade, hardened by years running freight on the fringes of settled space. Reliable and hard to rattle, he pilots a ship for Draxus Goods out of the auxiliary lot in Blackharbor, working alongside Callum Vex.

Appears in: Ep 5-6

npcs/jett-harlow.title: Jett Harlow
npcs/jett-harlow.content:
Jett Harlow is a gunslinger with a deadly calm and a darkly witty streak — reputation enough that he’s known as “the Viper.” He appeared in a flashback to a data vault heist, taking the job for the credits and because Nyx Verhoeven vouched for him. In the flashback, he was voiced by guest performer Doja. He was last seen alive during the crew’s escape from the vault.

Appears in: Ep 9

npcs/joran-red-veyne.title: Joran Red Veyne
npcs/joran-red-veyne.content:
Joran Red Veyne is a former Guardian soldier turned rebel leader, and the crew’s main contact within The Saltborn resistance in Blackharbor. Charismatic and resourceful, he didn’t simply defect from the Guardians — he built an organization, drawing capable, skilled people to his cause. Under his leadership, hope has begun to take root in Blackharbor despite the Guardians’ grip on the district.

Appears in: Ep 5-8

npcs/kano-rix.title: Kano Rix
npcs/kano-rix.content:
Kano Rix was an ex-convict and bank robber with a reputation for pulling off high-risk heists with cool precision — he’d robbed six banks and been caught only once, and even then his crew got away with the money. He found religion in prison, joining a Shinto-tech offshoot called Shintech, whose adherents believe machines carry kami — spirits — of their own; he performed a small ritual of respect before using any piece of technology. In prison he became Thorne’s only real friend, and the two stayed loyal to each other afterward.
Physically he was a shorter, lean man with coppery skin, a thin, grey-streaked beard, and a far-off, daydreaming look in his eyes. He wore low-profile streetwear patched with Shintech symbols and carried a carved wooden kitsune amulet on a leather cord, along with a worn lucky coin from his first big score, which he’d fiddle with, and he meditated often using the kitsune as a focus.
Kano accompanied Thorne to a meeting in the alley behind Club KuroLuxe in Polyphn, and fought alongside the group during the ensuing gravcar chase and the assault on The Relay Tower. He was killed during the Nexus assault there.

Appears in: Ep 13

npcs/lissara-holt.title: Lissara Holt
npcs/lissara-holt.content:
Lissara Holt is a scout and survivalist working with The Saltborn in Blackharbor. She knows every hidden passage in and out of the district, making her valuable for smuggling and evasion.

Appears in: Ep 5-8

npcs/mara-vex.title: Mara Vex
npcs/mara-vex.content:
Mara Vex is a survivor of the maglev crash in Bloc 6 that killed her family, and a driven infiltrator hunting the truth behind who was responsible. Nexus Corp officers arrived at the crash site and killed survivors; Mara escaped and was reported dead, her credit accounts frozen. She spent the following year off-grid piecing together evidence of a cover-up, and discovered that Sallerist had faked his own death in the crash.
Lean, wary, and calculating, Mara wears a heavily patched tactical jacket and keeps a photo of her family tucked inside it, along with her mother’s broken watch on her wrist. She’s quick to distrust and slow to open up — people either love her or want her dead, with little in between.
In Polyphn she allied with Thorne and the crew, backed by her bodyguard Brick and an old contact, the ripperdoc Dr. Sial, who had installed her cybernetic modifications: a telescopic ocular implant capable of zooming to 500 meters, and a “Ghost Talker” cochlear transceiver that let Sial see through her eyes and offer remote support. It was later revealed that Sial had been using that same link to feed Nexus Trading her location the whole time, which was how Nexus kept finding the group.
Mara fought alongside the crew during the gravcar chase and the subsequent assault on The Relay Tower.

Appears in: Ep 13

npcs/marshal-ulyx-carran.title: Marshal Ulyx Carran
npcs/marshal-ulyx-carran.content:
Marshal Ulyx Carran is the fanatical leader of the Guardians of the Great Work, ruling Blackharbor with an iron fist. He is utterly convinced that without the Great Work, civilization on Wafisa is doomed.

Appears in: Ep 3-6

npcs/marun.title: Brother Calyx
npcs/marun.content:
Brother Calyx was a void cultist stationed at Exosite 34b on Sibylen, part of the Void Cultists. He referred to himself in the third person by his cult title — “Old Brother Calyx has got himself a cat. This is the best day ever.” — and carried himself with a soldier’s bearing, dressed in heavy cult armor.
When the crew arrived at Exosite 34b, Brother Calyx was crouched petting Percy, the crew’s cat. Combat broke out, and after his partner was killed he tried to surrender, offering to explain himself and inviting the crew to join the Void Cult, calling it a source of purpose. When he refused to reveal why Rynn Kade was present at the site — declaring he’d rather die than betray the cult — Haleyy killed him.

Appears in: Ep 23

npcs/meer-prust.title: Meer Prust
npcs/meer-prust.content:
Meer Prust is the Second High Auctioneer Representative for Sibylen, a short, heavyset man with a white Hungarian mustache who wears the ceremonial robes of the Auctioneers Guild. An expert in bureaucracy and InterCorporate law, he holds offices in The Spigot.
He first appeared in Episode 21, arriving during Viktor Strake’s interrogation of the crew. Using his authority, he demanded Strake release Dr. Corbin as the auction representative for Laicar Research, then backed Thorne’s legal argument to secure the release of the entire crew for 24 hours — quietly telling Strake afterward, “After the auction, they’re all yours.”
Prust went on to conduct the auction for Exosite 34b. When Void Cultists attacked during the auction, he was captured and wired into the alien Fork alongside Vera Corbin and Sally Gaylen, his consciousness merging into the new entity known as The Concordant.

Appears in: Ep 21

npcs/michael--and--claire-harrow.title: Michael & Claire Harrow
npcs/michael--and--claire-harrow.content:
The Harrows were a family who perished during the collapse of Wafisa. The crew discovered their remains and belongings while exploring the Glendale Hotel.
Michael Harrow, who had worked in the financial sector before Wafisa’s fall, was found dead slumped over a writing desk in a locked room on the hotel’s fourth floor. He left behind recordings, letters, a laptop, a USB recording device, and clues pointing to a hidden machine and a family recipe book. His final recording warned any who found it: “If you find this, don’t stay here. Don’t wait. Don’t hunker down. Don’t try to wait it out. Leave this planet as soon as you can. There’s nothing left here for people like us.”
Claire Harrow, his wife, was found deceased in the bed of the same hotel room, her long blonde hair stringy with time. Michael had left behind a letter and a folder of photos dedicated to her, and her garnet amulet was found on the bedside table.
Their child, Liam Harrow, is unaccounted for. His room, found at 17 Millbrook Lane, was decorated with children’s toys and clown and dolphin motifs, and contained two decks of Lokipon Cards. His fate remains unknown.
Among the family’s belongings, the crew recovered a pre-collapse luxury hover car — the Aurora LX-90 — found in Millbrook Storage, a compact energy-cell handgun with an AI aiming system, the Harrow Family Cookbook, and a set of seventeen octagonal coppery-bronze coins bearing the insignia of the Guardians of the Great Work.

Appears in: Ep 5, Ep 6

npcs/nesso-tharn.title: Nesso Tharn
npcs/nesso-tharn.content:
Nesso Tharn was a former ship captain turned second-in-command of the Void Cultists cult operating out of Scrapjacks. A bald, pale man with piercing blue eyes, abnormally tall and gangly, he was tactical and stern, testing the faith of those around him like a drill sergeant.
Tharn confronted the crew at Scrapjacks in Episodes 10 and 11. The encounter ended with his death — killed by Haleyy, who punched him and drove his face into cement.

Appears in: Ep 10, Ep 11

npcs/nyx-verhoeven.title: Nyx Verhoeven
npcs/nyx-verhoeven.content:
Nyx Verhoeven, known in the underworld as Silentpaw, is a cat burglar — a perfectionist who dislikes violence. She appeared in a flashback in Episode 9, played by Steph, repaying a debt to Felix Champlin, who had once saved her life by rerouting medical drones to her.
Nyx has a signature calling card: she leaves small mouse figurines, nicknamed “Little Mice,” at the scenes of her heists. Jett Harlow has been quietly pocketing them after jobs and taking credit for her work rather than crediting Nyx.
She was last seen during the escape from a data vault heist.

Appears in: Ep 9

npcs/peter-haslow.title: Peter Haslow
npcs/peter-haslow.content:
Peter Haslow is a man in a silver suit who frequents The Vent bar in The Spigot. Bushy-bearded and bald, with wiry pale arms, he’s a competent mechanic who repairs bots in the dunes and scribes and installs ownership modules. Described by Dr. Iso as a self-described big-time snitch and “huge rat,” he’s nonetheless a nice guy at heart — and the two don’t get along. He ended up stuck on the Spigot years ago when a temporary job turned into a stable one and he could no longer afford the fare home.
He first appeared in Episode 25, when Thorne approached him at the Vent using the cover identity Tyson Fildar of Goodbot Electronics. Haslow agreed to sell information for 500 credits: the next autonomous shipment of ownership modules was due to arrive at Helium Docks #7 at 3am, unloaded entirely by bots with no human attendants. He was caught in a grenade blast at the Vent but survived, and was being questioned by Regulators as Thorne left the scene.

Appears in: Ep 25

npcs/petey-champlin.title: Petey Champlin
npcs/petey-champlin.content:
Petey Champlin is Felix Champlin’s younger brother, a journalist and former field medic who served in the Doppler Skirmishes. He worked for Blackout Press under the pen name “Dox Ryker,” acting as a mole inside Omnitek Holdings to investigate their prisoner conversion program, and spent several months at Omnitek itself under a “research assistant” cover identity.
His story was revealed in a flashback in Episode 9. During a heist on an orbital data vault, Petey was killed by a device that copies a person’s consciousness and destroys the body in the process. His body died, but an AI copy of his mind was left behind, trapped within Omnitek’s servers and subjected to nightmare testing simulations as part of a covert Omnitek program. Notably, Petey’s copy is an AI — a copied consciousness — rather than a true consciousness transfer like the one that created Dr. Elara Voss, where the original person continues to exist.
Freeing Petey is a central driver of Felix’s motivations.

Appears in: Ep 9

npcs/quartermaster-haelka-breen.title: Quartermaster Haelka Breen
npcs/quartermaster-haelka-breen.content:
Haelka Breen is the quartermaster who controls the rationing of food and supplies in Blackharbor on behalf of the Guardians of the Great Work, operating out of the Guardian Compound. Bribes and favoritism reportedly run rampant under her watch.

Appears in: Ep 3, Ep 4, Ep 5, Ep 6

npcs/reginald-froggy-vance.title: Reginald "Froggy" Vance
npcs/reginald-froggy-vance.content:
Reginald “Froggy” Vance — known for years over the airwaves as “The Voice of the Wastes” — is a companion of the crew of The Scapegoat. A man in his upper forties with a peculiar, frog-like demeanor — a lopsided walk, a habit of crouching slightly, a croaky voice, and a sickly greenish pallor — he was found hiding in the DJ booth of WK9078 Radio Station on Wafisa in Episode 6, where he’d spent fifteen years broadcasting to whoever would listen while trying (and failing) to fix the station’s generator.
Froggy was born on Wafisa in 2638. His father was killed in skirmishes with the Guardians of the Great Work when he was five, after which his mother took him to Blackharbor. There he met Vera Corbin, also five at the time, and the two grew up together until her family left for Sibylen when they were sixteen. They stayed in touch over the Exo-Net until the Guardians shut it down on Wafisa, cutting off contact for twenty-five years. Froggy’s mother died under harsh working conditions when he was twenty-five; he fled into the dead megacity that had once been Wafisa’s capital and lived as a hermit for seven years before finding the radio station and settling in. He kept a pet rat, Ratty, for four years; Ratty’s death left him in true isolation for a year before the crew found him.
The crew helped repair his radio tower, and he joined the crew of the Scapegoat around Episodes 6-7. He was shot in the chest by Omnitek Holdings soldiers shortly after and stabilized with a Lazarus patch by Robert. Aboard ship, he keeps a hidden living space tucked into the cargo bay, and secretly owns a cat named Percy, picked up as a kitten from a truck stop without the rest of the crew’s knowledge. He enjoys playing with Robert’s Lokipon cards, though his habit of licking his fingers and crumpling them tends to ruin the deck, and he struggles with anxiety underground.
After the Void Cultists attack on the Sibylen auction in Episode 21, Froggy retreated to his room, badly shaken, and was turned Unhallowed during the chaos. In Episode 23, the crew found him zombified in the exosite goo pool room, eyes blank and face wet with tears, carrying alien debris under the direction of Rynn Kade. When Haleyy discovered she could command the Unhallowed, she ordered Froggy to sit in a corner and gave him the task of looking after his cat, Percy — he followed the direct order, though verbal commands alone couldn’t snap him fully out of the Unhallowed state.
As of Episode 28, Froggy remains Unhallowed, refusing to leave his nest aboard the ship and repeatedly calling out for Vera. Dr. Iso has been unable to get through to him. The Concordant — the entity that now contains Vera’s merged consciousness — is aboard the ship under lock by Felix. Amid the tension, Robert asked Iso to cut off Froggy’s hands if he touched the Lokipon cards again, prompting Thorne to defend him.
Froggy’s fear and fragility have become something of an emotional barometer for the crew — a measure of just how bad things have gotten since Sibylen.

Appears in: Ep 6, Ep 7, Ep 21, Ep 23, Ep 28

npcs/roger-neronta.title: Roger Neronta
npcs/roger-neronta.content:
Roger Neronta is a guard with the Neon Fangs and owner of Roger’s Billiards, a five-table pool hall on Camiri 4 in Neon Fangs Territory. Extremely generous — sometimes to a fault, according to his wife — he gives back to his community more than he probably should.
His wife Cecelia works the bar, and his eldest son Axel loves rock music. Roger appeared in Episode 1, where he returned credits to Haleyy out of pure kindness, telling her: “My friend, whatever’s happening, it will get better. It will. Just stay with your friends. They’re a good lot.”

Appears in: Ep 1

npcs/rynn-kade.title: Rynn Kade
npcs/rynn-kade.content:
Rynn Kade was an agent of Nexus Trading who first appeared in Episode 21 on Sibylen. Already “untethered” — aligned with the Void Cultists but not yet turned Unhallowed — she attempted to secure Exosite 34b through the auction. When she failed to win it, her cultist allies attacked.
The crew later found her within the exosite complex, directing Unhallowed laborers. She was killed in Episode 24 at Exosite 34b, shot by Robert Ross after she put a bullet through Thorne’s chest, leaving him at the brink of death.

Appears in: Ep 21, Ep 24

npcs/sada-korva.title: Sada Korva
npcs/sada-korva.content:
Sada Korva, known as “The Flint,” is an explosives expert and key member of The Saltborn rebellion in Blackharbor. Once a miner forced into labor camps run by the Guardians of the Great Work, she now fights against them.

Appears in: Ep 5, Ep 6, Ep 7, Ep 8

npcs/sally-gaylen.title: Sally Gaylen
npcs/sally-gaylen.content:
Sally Gaylen is a tech expert working for Virodyne Labs, present on Sibylen for the auction of Exosite 34b. She carried insider knowledge of Virodyne’s operations.
During the Void Cultists attack on the auction in Episode 17, Gaylen was captured along with Vera Corbin and Meer Prust. All three were wired to Paracausal Bifurcation Array, the alien device at the heart of the exosite, and their minds were merged by void energy into a single new intelligence: The Concordant.

Appears in: Ep 17

npcs/thalia.title: Thalia
npcs/thalia.content:
Thalia Draxus is Thorne’s mother and the former CEO of Draxus Goods, the family company he grew up expecting to inherit. Sharp, calculating, and driven above all by protecting the company she built, she has proven willing to make devastating unilateral choices in its name.
Years before the crew’s journey began, William Sallerist was running a smuggling ring inside Draxus Goods’ operations. Worried about her son’s increasingly reckless involvement, Thalia planted evidence implicating both Thorne and Sallerist, intending for both to be removed from the picture. The plan backfired badly: Thorne took the full ten-year sentence while Sallerist escaped blame, then used the company’s collapsed credibility to sell it off cheap to Nexus Trading once he took over as managing director. Thalia spent the following decade trying to reclaim what she’d lost.
Thalia resurfaced in Episode 13, “Nexus of Betrayal: Thorne’s Story.” She anonymously contacted Thorne with a cipher key and instructions to meet Mara Vex, having also arranged Mara’s side of the encounter. She then confronted Thorne atop The Relay Tower, dressed head to toe in black, and revealed the truth he had never known: that it was her, not Sallerist alone, who had framed him. She claimed to have spent the ten years since trying to undo what she’d done, and offered Thorne her resources and information going forward. In the chaos that followed, she vanished up the tower’s stairs before the fighting ended — her means of escape a mystery to this day.

Appears in: Ep 13

npcs/the-concordant.title: The Concordant
npcs/the-concordant.content:
The Concordant is a new Virtual Intelligence born from “The Joining” — the forced merger of three human minds through the alien Paracausal Bifurcation Array and void energy. It’s housed in a silver orb similar to Dr. Elara Voss’s.
The three component minds are Vera Corbin, a xenoarchaeologist with Laicar Research; Meer Prust, Second High Auctioneer Representative of the Auctioneers Guild; and Sally Gaylen, a tech expert employed by Virodyne Labs. All three personalities, memories, and thoughts are retained within the orb — they communicate with each other at incredible speed, functioning as one being while remaining distinct individuals.
The Concordant was created during Episode 17, in the chaos of a Void Cultists attack on Sibylen. Since then it has gone inert and silent, and has been locked away by Felix Champlin aboard The Scapegoat.

Appears in: Ep 17

npcs/torik-rustclaw-sarr.title: Torik Rustclaw Sarr
npcs/torik-rustclaw-sarr.content:
Torik Rustclaw Sarr — known simply as Rustclaw — was a hulking, heavily scarred figure who grew up in the industrial zones of Camiri 4. His nickname came from his brutal fighting style and a mechanical cybernetic claw. Known for his strength and commanding presence, he led the Drift Rats gang and fancied himself something of a poet (“Docking Bay 72, look at me, I’m a poet.”)
The crew first encountered Rustclaw in Episode 1 and did him a favor. In Episode 2, once the job was done, he betrayed them, attempting to steal their ship as they prepared to leave. Robert Ross killed him with a critical headshot from a combat rifle during the ensuing space chase.

Appears in: Ep 1, Ep 2

npcs/vera-corbin.title: Vera Corbin
npcs/vera-corbin.content:
Vera Corbin is a xenoarchaeologist, the last remaining employee of Laicar Research on Sibylen, and an old friend of Froggy from childhood. Excitable and driven, she was in her upper forties when the crew met her.
She was born on Wafisa and moved to Sibylen with her family as a teenager. She began working for Laicar Research young, which gave her access to the Exo-Net and let her reconnect with Froggy — contact that was later severed for twenty-five years after the Guardians shut the network down on Wafisa. Over the following decades she helped build Laicar Research and became a part owner, but by the time the crew arrived the company was down to about five employees and going bankrupt.
The crew met Vera in Episode 14 at Laicar’s research station on Sibylen, after Froggy — whom they had kept alive since he was shot in Episode 7 — asked them to deliver her a message. It was an emotional reunion; she still calls him “Reginald.” Vera had discovered Exosite 34b, a buried alien quarantine facility, and had been excavating it for about eighteen months. She identified alien inscriptions in the facility as patterns associated with medical or healing structures, and saw the site’s upcoming auction as Laicar Research’s last chance at survival. She struck a contract with Thorne, giving Scapegoat Solutions LLC a cut of any auction discoveries in exchange for the crew’s help. When the exosite’s door activated for the first time, she marveled: “This might be the first example of alien technology actually activating. You have no idea what this means.”
In Episode 15, she helped the crew explore the deeper levels of the quarantine facility. But in Episode 17, during the auction, Void Cultists attacked and captured her along with Meer Prust and Sally Gaylen. All three were wired to Paracausal Bifurcation Array and merged by void energy into a single new intelligence, The Concordant.

Appears in: Ep 14, Ep 15, Ep 17

npcs/victor-saren.title: Victor Saren
npcs/victor-saren.content:
Victor Saren is the digital CEO of Omnitek Holdings, encountered by Felix Champlin in the flashback recounting his origin in Episode 9, “Brother’s Keeper: Felix’s Story.” Saren appeared as a digital presence rather than a man in the room, manifesting to defend Omnitek’s orbital data vault above Polyphn with a set of telescopic restraint arms when Felix, his brother Petey Champlin, and the rest of their crew — Nyx Verhoeven and Jett Harlow — broke in.
The vault held evidence of Operation Red Wing, an Omnitek program that purchased prisoners and used them as test subjects for digitizing human consciousness. During the heist, Petey’s own consciousness was captured and trapped within Omnitek’s servers. Felix escaped, but was forced to burn his old identity, change his name, and later infiltrate Omnitek itself hoping to find a way to rescue his brother. Killing Victor Saren has been one of Felix’s core, driving motivations ever since.

Appears in: Ep 9

npcs/viktor-strake.title: Viktor Strake
npcs/viktor-strake.content:
Viktor Strake is Virodyne Labs’s top risk management officer — a ruthless enforcer tasked with protecting the corporation’s interests at any cost. A genetically modified human, he carries a spotless professional record and something of a reputation in Virodyne circles: “Everyone knows Victor.”
He’s easy to pick out of a crowd: shaven sides with long blond hair on top, brown eyes, a square-cut jaw, and a jet-black Virodyne Labs uniform trimmed in white. His manner is cocky, arrogant, and theatrical — the kind of man who slow-claps and grins even while losing.
Strake is a recurring thorn in the crew’s side, and there’s a standing mystery around just how many of him there are. Felix Champlin killed a Strake on the bridge of The Scapegoat, only for what appeared to be the same man to be seen exiting a stealth fighter moments later. His ship, The Acceptable Loss, has been found carrying one or two duplicate bodies in stasis — whether these are clones, backups, or something else has never been explained on-air.
He first appeared in Episodes 7-8, arriving at Wafisa aboard a triangular stealth ship with a small team of Omnitek Holdings soldiers, having traced the crew by following Dr. Elara Voss’s hack when her power went down. He caught up with them at Blackharbor shortly after.
In Episode 18, a Strake (or a duplicate) attacked the crew at the Helium Docks on The Spigot with a squad of drones.
He resurfaced in the Episode 20 epilogue, looming over an unconscious Haleyy as she briefly stirred — “I had no idea how valuable you were” — while the rest of the crew, bound nearby, could only watch.
In Episode 21, Strake captured the crew at Sibylen, seized Dr. Elara Voss’s orb, and locked the crew inside their own ship using Omnitek’s admin override codes.
By Episode 28, Causeway 3 transit logs — recovered by Felix from the first security layer of the Causeway 3 server room — confirmed that The Acceptable Loss had passed through the routing station en route to Prometheon Technologies, with Voss still aboard.
Strake’s known gear includes a laser pistol and a physical Virodyne admin key capable of locking down The Scapegoat and handing Virodyne control of the ship.

Appears in: Ep 7, Ep 8, Ep 18, Ep 20, Ep 21, Ep 28

npcs/william-sallerist.title: William Sallerist
npcs/william-sallerist.content:
William Sallerist is the man Thorne spent years believing had destroyed his life. He was formerly the managing director of Draxus Goods, Thorne’s family company, after Nexus Trading absorbed it.
Sallerist had been running a smuggling ring within Nexus Trading’s operations. When Thalia Draxus planted evidence implicating both Thorne and Sallerist — hoping to remove them both from the company — Sallerist managed to shift the blame entirely onto Thorne, who was sentenced to ten years in prison. Sallerist then took over as managing director of Draxus Goods and pushed Thalia out entirely, running the company as a Nexus Trading subsidiary for roughly nine years.
About a year before Episode 13, Sallerist was declared dead in a maglev crash at Bloc 6 that killed twelve residents and five other occupants — Nexus officers moved in afterward to clean up survivors and complete the cover-up. In truth, he had faked his death and disappeared into hiding.
In Episode 13, “Nexus of Betrayal: Thorne’s Story,” Thorne uncovered proof from a data cache at The Relay Tower that Sallerist was still alive — proof that also revealed the deeper truth that it was actually Thalia Draxus, not Sallerist alone, who had framed him. As of that episode, Sallerist remains missing, his current whereabouts unknown to the crew.

Appears in: Ep 13

npcs/yana-7.title: Yana 7
npcs/yana-7.content:
Yana 7 is the owner and corporate representative of Scrap Jack’s Refueling and Grub, a fuel station in the Orus system. She wears a formal power suit and runs the station’s administrative office, managing day-to-day operations alongside the station AI, Buddy.
The crew met her in Episode 10 when they stopped at the station to refuel — weapons had to be left aboard ship per station policy. Shortly after, the Void Cultists took over the station and activated a void ansible, and Yana was swept up in the crisis alongside the crew and other station regulars. Over Episodes 11 and 12, the crew fought to retake the station, ultimately destroying the void rift and antenna and ending the incursion.
By the end of Episode 12, Yana and Thorne had struck up a romance; the two have kept in touch since via exo-mail. She’s spoken warmly of the Zephyran people, telling Thorne: “I have heard of Zephyrus. I heard that the people from there are known for their beauty.”

Appears in: Ep 10, Ep 11, Ep 12

pcs/felix-champlin.title: Felix Champlin
pcs/felix-champlin.content:
Felix Champlin is the hacker and communications specialist aboard The Scapegoat, played by Scott. Born in 2649 on New Lucerne, Felix has a prosthetic right leg (from the hip down) that causes him chronic pain, which he sometimes manages with drugs. He prefers machines to people, works from a foldout three-screen “data slab,” and is driven by one overriding goal: rescuing his brother.
Backstory
Felix’s younger brother, Petey Champlin, was a journalist and field medic working undercover for Blackout Press inside Omnitek Holdings, investigating the corporation’s prisoner conversion program under the pen name “Dox Ryker.” Felix, Petey, and two accomplices broke into Omnitek’s orbital data vault above Polyphn and discovered Operation Red Wing — Omnitek’s scheme to buy prisoner contracts, digitize the prisoners’ consciousness as AI test subjects, and kill the bodies in the process. Petey was killed during the heist by a device that copies consciousness and destroys the body; his digitized mind remains trapped in Omnitek’s servers, running through nightmare simulations.
Felix escaped, changed his face, voice, and name, and infiltrated Omnitek under a new identity to track the vault as it relocated. Roughly two years later, Felix — under his new identity — was assigned to an Omnitek unit called Echo 3, where he first met Thorne; the two ran several missions together before going their separate ways. Felix later hacked the mission applicant list that got him assigned to Dr. Elara Voss’s crew, not realizing she had already selected him independently — his goal in joining was to reach the vault, now relocated near Prometheon Technologies Station.
Powers and Growth
During the crew’s exploration of an alien digital space, Felix received knowledge directly from Dr. Elara Voss, gaining a bonus to his technical skill that applies specifically to alien-tech interfaces. He can manipulate alien gel-mold interfaces with his programming skill, and made a working copy of Buddy AI’s source code and personality after hacking it at Scrapjacks — that copy has since helped run the Scapegoat’s systems.
Gear
Felix carries a stun baton, a knife, and a Stauser pistol, and wears Secure Clothing for armor. His readied gear includes his dataslab, a line shunt, and a metatool.
Character Spotlights
Free Patreon bonus content exploring Felix’s early life covers his childhood discovery of a gift for hardware at a coastal electronics dump, and a teenage repair of his neighborhood’s water reclaimer that shaped his belief that systems fail because people stop asking the right questions.

Appears in: Ep 1, 9, 10, 11, 15, 18

pcs/haleyy.title: Haleyy
pcs/haleyy.content:
Haleyy is the crew’s muscle and biopsionic aboard The Scapegoat, played by Steph. Born in 2658 on Vigrid, a desert world in the Thraxis system, she loves beer and fighting, and carries a tough, direct manner shaped by a complicated past she didn’t fully understand until recently. Her eyes are green, though they were originally brown before an incident on Ventos.
Early Life
Haleyy grew up training alone on Vigrid: fighting, week-long desert survival runs armed with only kitchen knives, and building improvised workout equipment her parents never noticed. That conditioning became the foundation of her physical toughness. Early in her military career, she and a partner were stranded at an open airlock as their ship drifted away; Haley jumped without hesitation, while her partner hesitated and was lost.
True Identity
Haleyy’s true identity was revealed to the crew at The Spigot: she is Haley, with one Y — the “Haleyy” persona, and the story of a missing sister named Haley, never existed as a separate person. During a mission on Ventos, she was struck by energy from an alien fork inside a cave and killed during the escape, then revived in the morgue by a biopsionic healing ability she didn’t know she had. She woke with no memory of her death, having unconsciously constructed a new identity and a cover story casting “Haley with one Y” as an older sister who had gone missing. Robert Ross, who served with the real Haley, knew the truth the whole time. The two identities merged into a single, whole sense of self after a psychic dream sequence in Episode 20, in which a vision of “Haley” told her plainly: “Your sister is not missing. You are an only child.”
Biopsionic Powers
Haleyy has been struck by void or alien-fork energy multiple times: first on Ventos (in flashback), again by a void tendril at Scrapjacks, and a third time during an exosite fork activation on Sibylen. These contacts unlocked bio-electromagnetic and healing abilities, which first activated involuntarily in Episode 24 when she healed Thorne’s gunshot wound during the auction finale, collapsing from the exertion immediately afterward. A brain scan in Episode 23 detected crystalline micro-structures throughout her brain alongside other physiological changes, later confirmed to be progressing toward a dangerous full-consumption timeline. The Void Cultists have identified her as “untethered” — someone who has touched the void naturally, without their ritual.
Gear
Haleyy fights with a revolver, a large advanced weapon, a laser rifle, and her bare hands, wearing Woven Body Armor. She carries a broken, decades-old military data pad she believes belonged to her sister, an analog notepad since the pad doesn’t work, a deck of Lokipon Cards she keeps despite being a poor player, and the Harrow Family Cookbook, which she has carried since Wafisa.
Character Spotlights
Free Patreon bonus content covers Haleyy’s endurance during military training, her first offworld missions for Omnitek, and a letter home from her earliest days in service.

Appears in: Ep 10, 11, 18, 19, 20, 21, 23, 24, 28

pcs/robert-ross.title: Robert Ross
pcs/robert-ross.content:
Robert Ross is the pilot aboard The Scapegoat, played by Doja. He has an afro, loves chaos, and often creates more problems through his “helping” than he solves — but he surprised even himself by choosing to stay with the crew instead of running, coming to see them as family.
True Identity
Robert is clone RR7, part of an experimental squadron created by Virodyne Labs through Omnitek Holdings at a cloning facility in the Omnitek-controlled section of Polyphn. Lab-grown and brought to full size within months, he was fitted with Kinetika Dynamics weaponry and armor before the clone program was scrapped following the disaster on Ventos. Clones like Robert have unique memories implanted at random during creation — everything in his life before his first real mission, including his backstory about being scammed out of his savings, was randomly generated content that coalesced into the personality he now has.
Strike Force 6
Robert’s squad was delivered to Vigrid for training, where Haley (with one Y) was assigned as squad leader and Robert became her second-in-command. Sent with the rest of Strike Force 6 to Ventos during the Red Rice Wars, the squad located an alien structure containing a fork inside a cave system while rescuing Haley from captivity. Haley was struck by the fork’s energy, and one squadmate died during the escape. Fleeing on stolen motorcycles, the squad called for extraction — but an anti-air mech shot their helicopter out of the sky, killing two more squadmates. Robert found Haley mortally wounded and applied Lazarus patch after Lazarus patch trying to save her, only to realize she had already been dead for minutes. He was later assigned to watch over the amnesiac “Haleyy” who woke in her place, and has carried the truth of who she really is ever since.
Gear
Robert fights with a combat rifle and a laser pistol, keeps a brass-knuckle knife hidden in his boot, and wears Woven Body Armor. He has a bionic eye purchased at great cost from Nexus Trading, and collects Lokipon Cards despite being a poor player.
Character Spotlights
Free Patreon bonus content covers Robert’s beliefs, a small kindness Haley once showed him, and moments of him acting against his own instincts.

Appears in: Ep 18, 19

pcs/thorne.title: Thorne
pcs/thorne.content:
Thorne is the captain of The Scapegoat, played by Brian. Born in 2646 on Zephyrus Three, he’s a dignified businessman who loves music and songwriting, and serves as the crew’s voice and negotiator. Once reckless, he has grown measured and protective of his crew.
Backstory
Thorne’s full name is Thorne Draxus. His family owned Draxus Goods, a trading company run for five generations out of Zephyrus Three. A smuggling ring operating within the company led Thorne’s mother, Thalia Draxus, to plant evidence implicating both Thorne and the company’s William Sallerist, expecting both to go to prison. Instead, Sallerist escaped justice, shifted the blame entirely onto Thorne, and took over Draxus Goods as managing director under Nexus Trading. Thorne served roughly ten years of a twelve-year sentence before his contract was purchased by Omnitek Holdings.
After his release, Thorne was posted to Polyphn, where during a month of downtime he tracked down Sallerist’s fate, only to discover Sallerist had faked his death in a maglev crash. With help from allies he made on Polyphn, Thorne recovered proof of the fraud from a relay tower — but an informant betrayed them to Nexus, costing him two of those allies and getting a third captured, while his mother confirmed the truth at the tower’s summit. Around this same period, Thorne was assigned to an Omnitek unit called Echo 3, where he first met Felix Champlin; the two ran missions together before parting ways, reuniting later at Camiri 4.
Legal Genius
In Episode 17, when Viktor Strake captured the crew, Thorne used InterCorporate policy to argue they were technically Laicar Research employees under a legally binding contract with Scapegoat Solutions LLC — the legal entity he founded — forcing Strake to release them for 24 hours.
Personality and Relationships
Thorne’s love of music has become a defining trait, extending into an entire in-universe music lore he shares recommendations about with Reginald “Froggy” Vance. He collects Lokipon Cards and is a skilled player. He struck up a romantic relationship with a woman named Yana 7 at Scrapjacks, exchanging exo-mail with her. His overriding goal is to find William Sallerist and reclaim Draxus Goods.
In Episode 29, Thorne was dropped to just 2 of his 12 hit points shielding Felix from a drone swarm at Causeway 3.
Gear
Thorne carries a laser pistol and a laser rifle, and wears an Armored Undersuit. Among his personal effects are a leather driving jacket won in a card game and his father’s wedding ring, inscribed with the Drax family name.
Character Spotlights
Free Patreon bonus content covers Thorne’s favorite memory, his fears, a secret from his home world of Zephyrus Three, and his sense of familial responsibility.

Appears in: Ep 1, 2, 3, 13, 17, 29

ships/the-acceptable-loss.title: The Acceptable Loss
ships/the-acceptable-loss.content:
The Acceptable Loss is Viktor Strake’s personal ship, first encountered in Episode 7. Triangular, with three bird-like landing legs, it has the silhouette of a stealth jet. It carries one or two clone bodies in stasis at all times, kept in reserve for Strake’s use.

Appears in: Ep 7

ships/the-kid.title: The Kid
ships/the-kid.content:
The Kid is a small Omnitek shuttle the crew captured at The Spigot spaceport in Episode 18. Built to transport two people on long trips (or squeeze in four on short ones), it can be stored inside The Scapegoat’s cargo hold, taking up about an eighth of the total space, though it cannot be launched mid-flight from a frigate.
Formerly registered under Omnitek as Life Is Unfair, the crew renamed it after capture; its ownership module is still locked to Omnitek and needs replacing.
When the crew found it, the shuttle held a Robert Ross clone claiming to be alone, though evidence suggested a second occupant had been aboard. Orders found on the shuttle instructed its crew to follow, then eliminate, the PCs. Loot recovered aboard included several thousand credits, an encrypted datapad, a spike thrower, and a set of security armor.

Appears in: Ep 18

ships/the-scapegoat.title: The Scapegoat
ships/the-scapegoat.content:
The Scapegoat is the crew’s ship, a standard Free Merchant-class frigate with a couple of low-power weapons and a lot of cargo space — nothing special on paper. The crew named it in Episode 2, choosing “Scapegoat” over other candidates (Wayfarer, Serendipity, Quicksilver, The Deathstick, Argo) because of the connotations it carries for both Robert Ross and Thorne’s backstories — both feel like scapegoats in their own way.
History
Before falling into obscurity, the Scapegoat ran a regular supply route between Polyphn and Camiri 4, hauling scientific equipment, food, and other supplies. It was docked at Camiri 4 during the rebellion roughly twenty years ago, having just delivered a cargo of scientific equipment from Polyphn. When the station was overrun and the corporations pulled out, the ship was left locked behind the doors of Docking Bay 72 for the next two decades, until the crew found it.
Description
Roughly 100 yards long and 30-40 yards wide at its broadest, the Scapegoat is longer and narrower than ships like the Millennium Falcon or Serenity — built more like a spine with cargo bays hanging off it. It reads as a working truck rather than a starfighter: nobody in a dockyard looks at it twice. Its layout runs from the bridge at the bow, back along a central corridor of crew quarters and common spaces, to two cargo bays at the stern — the first housing The Aurora and Reginald “Froggy” Vance’s living space, the second largely empty and able to hold a small fighter.
It carries a multifocal laser and a sandthrower for weapons, 120 tons of pressurized cargo space, a hidden smuggler’s hold, and a burst ECM generator that can negate one successful hit against it.
Current Status
As of Episode 23, the Scapegoat has taken damage: its hull has a hole in it, its spike drive guidance is fried, and its ownership module needs a black-market replacement. Its security module was overwritten with Omnitek admin code by Viktor Strake, and Dr. Elara Voss’s VI reprogramming left its physical controls broken, requiring an autonomous system to manage them — a role now filled by Buddy AI, a copy Felix Champlin made of a hacked AI’s source code. Voss herself was taken from the ship in Episode 17; she had encoded a secret heading toward Prometheon Technologies into one of Strake’s communications before her capture.

ships/the-thalia.title: The Thalia
ships/the-thalia.content:
The Thalia is a two-person hauler, originally part of the Draxus Goods fleet and now running the old Draxus trade route under Nexus Trading control, crewed by Callum Vex and Harlan Rigg. Its route runs from Wafisa to Polyphn to Zephryss III, carrying alien artifacts recovered from Blackharbor and Wafisa to be processed and sold. It’s currently parked in the auxiliary lot of the Rust Yards in Blackharbor.
The ship is named after Thalia Draxus — Thorne’s mother, and the woman who handed Draxus Goods over to Nexus Trading. The ship predates that takeover; only the name stuck.

Appears in: Ep 13

timeline.title: Season 1 So Far
timeline.content:
Dark Star Adventurecast follows four expendable Omnitek contractors recruited by Dr. Elara Voss — ostensibly to investigate a mysterious signal out in deep space. Voss’s real agenda, revealed early on, is much bigger: she is the sector’s only Virtual Intelligence, and she’s using the crew to reach and strike at whatever Prometheon Technologies is secretly building — payback against Virodyne Labs, the mega-corp that experimented on her homeworld. What follows is the story of how a crew of strangers thrown together on a smuggling job became a found family chasing that signal across half a dozen worlds.
Camiri 4 — recruitment
The crew is assembled on Camiri 4 for a classified operation and has to fight and bluff their way out of Drift Rats territory just to get their hands on a ship, surviving a betrayal and a space chase in the process. They name the ship The Scapegoat — a name that turns out to fit.
Wafisa — the fabricated mission unravels
On Wafisa, the crew finds a world gone eerily quiet: an abandoned spaceport, the predatory Guardians of the Great Work, and a station slowly filling with methane. Sheltering at the Glendale Hotel, they piece together the fate of a family who lived through the planet’s collapse, and that trail leads them to Reginald Froggy Vance, a broadcaster holed up at a radio station, who becomes an ally and eventually a crewmate. When Viktor Strake and a squad of Omnitek soldiers show up hunting them, the crew is forced to flee to Blackharbor and fight their way back to their ship. In the aftermath, Dr. Elara Voss finally tells the truth: she isn’t the human scientist she appeared to be, but a Virtual Intelligence in an alien orb, and the whole mission was fabricated to get the crew moving toward her real target. She offers each of them a personal reason to keep going anyway, and they take the deal.
Scrapjacks — the void cult
A routine fuel stop at Scrapjacks turns into a siege when the Void Cultists seize the station and activate a void ansible. The fight introduces the crew — and the audience — to the Unhallowed and to void energy itself, and ends with the cult’s leadership dead and the rift destroyed. It’s here that Haleyy is first singled out by the cultists as “untethered,” a label that will come to matter a great deal later on.
Backstories: Felix and Thorne
Along the way, the crew’s two focus episodes so far pull back the curtain on where two of them came from. Felix Champlin’s story reveals a brother, Petey Champlin, trapped as a digitized consciousness inside Omnitek’s servers under a program called Operation Red Wing — the reason Felix burned his old identity and started over. Thorne’s story is a neo-noir detective tale about Nexus Trading stealing his family’s company, and ends with the gutting reveal that his own mother was behind his downfall, not the rival he’d spent years blaming.
Sibylen — the exosite and the Fork
The crew’s stay on Sibylen becomes the longest and strangest leg of the journey. Guided by xenoarchaeologist Vera Corbin, they descend into a buried alien structure called Exosite 34b, where they connect to an alien network, fight off self-replicating nano-fluid horrors, and eventually activate an ancient device called the Paracausal Bifurcation Array — opening a window across space to a five-ringed structure turning like a celestial gyroscope: Prometheon Station. Two more focus episodes land back to back here. Robert Ross’s story reveals he’s a clone, one of a squadron sent years earlier to rescue a woman named Haley from an alien-touched captivity on Ventos — a mission that ended in nearly everyone’s deaths. And Haleyy’s own focus episode takes the crew inside her unconscious mind, where a fractured identity finally reunites: Haleyy and the Haley from Robert’s story are the same person, and she wakes whole.
She doesn’t wake to safety, though. Viktor Strake captures the crew coming out of the exosite, and an auction over rights to Exosite 34b is torn apart when the Void Cultists attack, ritually fusing three people — including Vera — into a new entity called The Concordant. Strake stripped the crew of their ship’s ownership module and made off with Voss herself. Getting her back means storming the cultists’ own foothold in the exosite, where the crew discovers Haleyy can command the Unhallowed, and where a desperate last stand costs several cultist lives and nearly costs Thorne’s — saved only when Haleyy manifests a latent healing power of her own, a biosionic ability nobody knew she had. The Fork claims its captives anyway, and the inert orb it produces becomes the second Concordant to come out of Sibylen.
The Spigot — clones and a stolen module
Battered and short a Virtual Intelligence, the crew makes for The Spigot to get Haleyy medical attention and find a black-market replacement for their ship’s ownership module. There they meet Dr. Iso, who turns out — to everyone’s shock — to be another clone from Robert’s own line. The Spigot arc is defined by an escalating shadow war against more Omnitek-line clones sent to track the crew down, culminating in a heist on a Helium Docks shipment that finally gets them their module back, at the cost of a running gunfight and a lot of collateral damage. Iso joins the crew for good, and with Voss gone, Felix brings the ship’s old managing AI, Buddy, back online to keep The Scapegoat running.
Causeway 3 — the trail to Prometheon
With coordinates Voss had hidden inside one of Strake’s own transmissions, the crew makes an eighteen-day journey to an unlisted station called Causeway 3. Getting inside means talking, hacking, and bluffing their way past security, but it pays off: they confirm that The Acceptable Loss carried both Strake and Voss to Prometheon Station, and they turn up an older, deeper trail suggesting an Omnitek data vault made the same one-way trip years before. The discovery comes at a cost — the station’s security turns hostile, and the crew has to fight off swarms of drones just to get back to their ship and start the drill toward Prometheon, with a faster security vessel already closing in behind them as they go.
That’s where things stand as of Episode 29: a battered but intact crew, a confirmed destination, and pursuers on their tail. Catch up episode by episode on the Episode Guide.
